<content>
1: # llm-go
2: 
3: A Go port of the LLM handling layer from [opencode](https://github.com/sst/opencode).
4: Provides streaming LLM conversations, agentic tool-call orchestration, automatic
5: context compaction, and a pluggable knowledge retrieval system — all as composable
6: Go packages.
7: 
8: ```
9: github.com/larryhou/llm-go
10: ```
11: 
12: ---
13: 
14: ## Features
15: 
16: - **Streaming client with retry** — provider-agnostic `llm.Provider` interface;
17:   automatic retry with exponential back-off on transient errors; mid-stream error
18:   recovery without losing buffered events.
19: 
20: - **Two provider adapters** — `provider/anthropic` (official SDK) and
21:   `provider/openai` (OpenAI-compatible, works with any proxy or local endpoint).
22: 
23: - **Full agentic loop** (`session.RunLoop`) — user message → LLM stream →
24:   parallel tool execution → tool results back to LLM → repeat until `stop`.
25: 
26: - **Context compaction** — when the session approaches the model's context limit,
27:   the oldest turns are summarised by a second LLM call and replaced by a compact
28:   summary, then the conversation continues seamlessly.
29: 
30: - **Doom-loop detection** — stops the loop when the same tool is called with
31:   identical arguments three consecutive times.
32: 
33: - **Pluggable knowledge retrieval** (`knowledge.Manager`) — register any number
34:   of `Source` backends; the manager dispatches `knowledge_search` and
35:   `knowledge_fetch` as native `tool.Tool` calls, with priority grouping,
36:   concurrent dispatch per group, and automatic fallback.
37: 
38: - **Bleve full-text source** — ready-made `knowledge/source/bleve` backed by
39:   an in-memory or on-disk Bleve index.
40: 
41: - **HTTP knowledge API** (`cmd/llm-api`) — self-contained HTTP server
42:   that indexes a skills directory, exposes REST search/fetch endpoints, and
43:   streams LLM chat responses as Server-Sent Events.
44: 
45: - **opencode-compatible config** — reads `~/.config/llm/llm.json` and
46:   `.llm/llm.json`; schema mirrors opencode's `opencode.json`.
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## Package Layout
51: 
52: ```
53: github.com/larryhou/llm-go/
54: ├── llm/                  Canonical types, overflow math, error classification, retry
55: ├── provider/
56: │   ├── provider.go       Registry, Model, Info, ParseModel()
57: │   ├── anthropic/        Anthropic Messages API (anthropic-sdk-go)
58: │   └── openai/           OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions (openai-go)
59: ├── session/
60: │   ├── prompt.go         RunLoop() — main agentic loop
61: │   ├── processor.go      Event handler — tool lifecycle, doom-loop, overflow
62: │   ├── compaction.go     Compact() / Prune() / Select() / FilterCompacted()
63: │   ├── context.go        ToModelMessages() — store records → llm.Message
64: │   └── system.go         Per-provider embedded system prompts
65: ├── tool/                 Tool interface, ToolFailure, Registry, output truncation
66: ├── store/                Store interface (session / message / part CRUD)
67: │   └── memory/           In-memory Store implementation
68: ├── knowledge/            Manager, Source interface, knowledge_search/fetch tools
69: │   └── source/bleve/     Bleve-backed Source (Peek = snippets, Fetch = full doc)
70: ├── config/               Config schema, Load(), per-field accessors
71: ├── auth/                 auth.json reader/writer (oauth / api / wellknown)
72: └── cmd/
73:     ├── llm-api/    HTTP server — Bleve index + /chat SSE endpoint
74:     └── index-skills/     CLI — build an on-disk Bleve index from a skills directory
75: ```
76: 
77: ---
78: 
79: ## Quick Start
80: 
81: ### 1. Single-turn streaming call
82: 
83: ```go
84: package main
85: 
86: import (
87:     "context"
88:     "fmt"
89: 
90:     "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/llm"
91:     openaiProv "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/provider/openai"
92: )
93: 
94: func main() {
95:     prov := openaiProv.New(
96:         "sk-your-api-key",
97:         "https://api.openai.com/v1", // or any OpenAI-compatible URL
98:         "openai",
99:         nil,
100:     )
101:     client := llm.NewClient(prov)
102: 
103:     model := llm.Model{
104:         ID:         "gpt-4o",
105:         ProviderID: "openai",
106:         APIID:      "gpt-4o",
107:         Limit:      llm.ModelLimit{Context: 128_000, Output: 4096},
108:     }
109: 
110:     events := client.Stream(context.Background(), llm.Request{
111:         Model:    model,
112:         System:   []string{"You are a concise assistant."},
113:         Messages: []llm.Message{llm.NewUserMessage("What is the capital of France?")},
114:     })
115: 
116:     for ev := range events {
117:         if ev.IsText() {
118:             fmt.Print(ev.Text)
119:         }
120:     }
121:     fmt.Println()
122: }
123: ```
124: 
125: ### 2. Multi-turn agentic session with tools
126: 
127: ```go
128: package main
129: 
130: import (
131:     "context"
132:     "fmt"
133:     "strconv"
134: 
135:     "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/llm"
136:     openaiProv "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/provider/openai"
137:     "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/session"
138:     "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/store/memory"
139:     "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/tool"
140: )
141: 
142: // calcTool evaluates simple arithmetic expressions.
143: type calcTool struct{}
144: 
145: func (calcTool) Name() string        { return "calc" }
146: func (calcTool) Description() string { return "Evaluate a math expression, e.g. '2 + 3 * 4'" }
147: func (calcTool) InputSchema() map[string]any {
148:     return map[string]any{
149:         "type":     "object",
150:         "required": []string{"expr"},
151:         "properties": map[string]any{
152:             "expr": map[string]any{"type": "string"},
153:         },
154:     }
155: }
156: func (calcTool) Execute(_ context.Context, input map[string]any) (tool.Result, error) {
157:     expr, _ := input["expr"].(string)
158:     // (real impl would parse the expression)
159:     return tool.Result{Output: "42", Title: "calc"}, nil
160: }
161: 
162: func main() {
163:     ctx := context.Background()
164:     st  := memory.New()
165:     prov := openaiProv.New("sk-your-api-key", "https://api.openai.com/v1", "openai", nil)
166: 
167:     model := llm.Model{
168:         ID: "gpt-4o", ProviderID: "openai", APIID: "gpt-4o",
169:         Limit: llm.ModelLimit{Context: 128_000, Output: 4096},
170:     }
171: 
172:     // Create a session in the store.
173:     sessID := "demo-session-1"
174:     _ = st.CreateSession(ctx, &store.Session{ID: sessID, Model: "openai/gpt-4o"})
175: 
176:     // Turn 1
177:     session.RunLoop(ctx, st, session.RunInput{
178:         SessionID: sessID,
179:         UserMsg:   "What is 123 * 456?",
180:         Model:     model,
181:         Provider:  prov,
182:         Tools:     []tool.Tool{calcTool{}},
183:     })
184: 
185:     // Turn 2 — history is loaded automatically from the store
186:     session.RunLoop(ctx, st, session.RunInput{
187:         SessionID: sessID,
188:         UserMsg:   "Double the result.",
189:         Model:     model,
190:         Provider:  prov,
191:         Tools:     []tool.Tool{calcTool{}},
192:     })
193: }
194: ```
195: 
196: ### 3. Cancellable turns with `RunLoopAsync`
197: 
198: `RunLoop` is synchronous and blocks until the turn completes. `RunLoopAsync`
199: returns a `*RunHandle` immediately, allowing the caller to cancel an in-flight
200: turn and start a new one without waiting for the old one to fully clean up.
201: 
202: **`RunHandle` fields:**
203: 
204: | Field | Description |
205: |-------|-------------|
206: | `Done <-chan struct{}` | Closed after full cleanup including Prune |
207: | `StoreDone <-chan struct{}` | Closed once store writes are complete (before Prune) — sufficient for the next turn to start safely |
208: | `Result RunResult` | Available after `<-Done` |
209: | `Err error` | Available after `<-Done` |
210: 
211: ```go
212: // Start a turn asynchronously.
213: h := session.RunLoopAsync(ctx, st, session.RunInput{
214:     SessionID: sessID,
215:     UserMsg:   "What is 123 * 456?",
216:     Model:     model,
217:     Provider:  prov,
218:     Tools:     []tool.Tool{calcTool{}},
219: })
220: 
221: // Cancel the turn (e.g. user pressed ESC or sent a new message).
222: h.Cancel()
223: <-h.Done // wait for full cleanup before reusing the session
224: 
225: // --- OR: start a new turn immediately, passing StoreDone as WaitFor.
226: // The new turn's goroutine starts right away but waits internally on
227: // prev.StoreDone before writing to the store, so no orphan records are
228: // created and history is always consistent.
229: h2 := session.RunLoopAsync(ctx, st, session.RunInput{
230:     SessionID: sessID,
231:     UserMsg:   "Actually, what is 789 * 321?",
232:     Model:     model,
233:     Provider:  prov,
234:     Tools:     []tool.Tool{calcTool{}},
235:     WaitFor:   h.StoreDone, // wait for store consistency, not full Prune
236: })
237: <-h2.Done
238: ```
239: 
240: **Typical HTTP server pattern** (cancel previous turn on new message):
241: 
242: ```go
243: var mu sync.Mutex
244: var activeHandle *session.RunHandle
245: 
246: func handleChat(userMsg string) {
247:     mu.Lock()
248:     prev := activeHandle
249:     if prev != nil {
250:         prev.Cancel()
251:     }
252:     var waitFor <-chan struct{}
253:     if prev != nil {
254:         waitFor = prev.StoreDone
255:     }
256:     h := session.RunLoopAsync(ctx, st, session.RunInput{
257:         SessionID: sessID,
258:         UserMsg:   userMsg,
259:         Model:     model,
260:         Provider:  prov,
261:         WaitFor:   waitFor,
262:     })
263:     activeHandle = h
264:     mu.Unlock()
265: 
266:     <-h.Done // keep SSE connection open until turn finishes
267: }
268: ```
269: 
270: Holding `mu` across `Cancel + RunLoopAsync + activeHandle =` ensures a third
271: concurrent request cannot observe a stale previous handle and race on the same
272: `StoreDone`.
273: 
274: ### 4. Knowledge retrieval (search + fetch)
275: 
276: ```go
277: import (
278:     "time"
279:     bleve "github.com/blevesearch/bleve/v2"
280:     "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/knowledge"
281:     blevesrc "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/knowledge/source/bleve"
282:     "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/session"
283: )
284: 
285: // Build an in-memory Bleve index.
286: idx, _ := bleve.NewMemOnly(bleve.NewIndexMapping())
287: _ = idx.Index("doc-1", map[string]any{
288:     "title":   "Go concurrency patterns",
289:     "content": "Goroutines, channels, select...",
290: })
291: 
292: // Create the manager with a Bleve source.
293: km := knowledge.NewManager(knowledge.ManagerConfig{
294:     SourceTimeout:   5 * time.Second,
295:     MaxResults:      5,
296:     SnippetMaxChars: 300,
297:     ContentMaxChars: 8000,
298: })
299: km.Register(blevesrc.New(idx, "docs", 0, nil))
300: 
301: // Attach knowledge tools to RunLoop — no other changes needed.
302: session.RunLoop(ctx, st, session.RunInput{
303:     SessionID: sessID,
304:     UserMsg:   "What do you know about Go concurrency?",
305:     Model:     model,
306:     Provider:  prov,
307:     Tools:     km.Tools(), // injects knowledge_search + knowledge_fetch
308: })
309: ```
310: 
311: ### 5. Session history recall + session_reset
312: 
313: After compaction, old messages are hidden from the LLM. `SessionHistorySource`
314: indexes them into a private Bleve index so the LLM can search them on demand.
315: `session_reset` lets the LLM wipe the session on user request.
316: 
317: ```go
318: package main
319: 
320: import (
321:     "context"
322:     "fmt"
323:     "log"
324:     "time"
325: 
326:     bleve "github.com/blevesearch/bleve/v2"
327:     "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/knowledge"
328:     blevesrc "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/knowledge/source/bleve"
329:     "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/llm"
330:     openaiProv "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/provider/openai"
331:     "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/session"
332:     "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/store"
333:     "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/store/memory"
334:     "github.com/larryhou/llm-go/tool"
335: )
336: 
337: func main() {
338:     ctx  := context.Background()
339:     st   := memory.New()
340:     prov := openaiProv.New("sk-your-api-key", "https://api.openai.com/v1", "openai", nil)
341:     model := llm.Model{
342:         ID: "gpt-4o", ProviderID: "openai", APIID: "gpt-4o",
343:         Limit: llm.ModelLimit{Context: 128_000, Output: 4096},
344:     }
345: 
346:     sessID := "demo-session-1"
347:     _ = st.CreateSession(ctx, &store.Session{ID: sessID, Model: "openai/gpt-4o"})
348: 
349:     // 1. SessionHistorySource — per-session, created once.
350:     //    Priority 0 (highest): queried before static knowledge sources.
351:     //    maxCompactions=8 caps memory at ~50 MB per session.
352:     historySrc, err := knowledge.NewSessionHistorySource(sessID, knowledge.DefaultMaxCompactions)
353:     if err != nil {
354:         log.Fatal(err)
355:     }
356:     compactionHook := historySrc.Hook() // cache the hook, don't call Hook() per turn
357: 
358:     // 2. Knowledge manager — register static source at priority 1, history at 0.
359:     idx, _ := bleve.NewMemOnly(bleve.NewIndexMapping())
360:     km := knowledge.NewManager(knowledge.ManagerConfig{
361:         SourceTimeout: 5 * time.Second,
362:         MaxResults:    5,
363:         SnippetMaxChars: 300,
364:         ContentMaxChars: 8000,
365:     })
366:     km.Register(blevesrc.New(idx, "docs", 1, nil))
367:     km.Register(historySrc) // history has higher priority (0)
368: 
369:     // 3. session_reset tool — resetFn is called atomically.
370:     //    If a server-level lock is needed (concurrent requests), hold it here.
371:     resetTool := session.NewResetTool(func(resetCtx context.Context) error {
372:         if err := st.DeleteSession(resetCtx, sessID); err != nil {
373:             return err
374:         }
375:         if err := st.CreateSession(resetCtx, &store.Session{
376:             ID: sessID, Model: "openai/gpt-4o",
377:         }); err != nil {
378:             return err
379:         }
380:         return historySrc.Reset() // wipes the Bleve index
381:     })
382: 
383:     // 4. Build tool list — explicit make avoids aliasing km.Tools() backing array.
384:     kmTools := km.Tools()
385:     tools := make([]tool.Tool, 0, len(kmTools)+1)
386:     tools = append(tools, kmTools...)
387:     tools = append(tools, resetTool)
388: 
389:     // 5. RunLoop — pass OnCompact so compacted turns are indexed automatically.
390:     for _, msg := range []string{
391:         "Explain context compaction.",
392:         "What did we discuss earlier?", // LLM may call knowledge_search here
393:     } {
394:         _, err := session.RunLoop(ctx, st, session.RunInput{
395:             SessionID: sessID,
396:             UserMsg:   msg,
397:             Model:     model,
398:             Provider:  prov,
399:             Tools:     tools,
400:             OnCompact: compactionHook, // nil = no history indexing
401:         })
402:         if err != nil {
403:             fmt.Fprintf(nil, "error: %v\n", err)
404:         }
405:     }
406: }
407: ```
408: 
409: **Key rules:**
410: - Create `SessionHistorySource` and call `Hook()` **once per session**, not per turn.
411: - Register `historySrc` at a **lower priority number** than static knowledge sources.
412: - Build `tools` with explicit `make` + `append` — do not `append(km.Tools(), ...)` directly.
413: - The `resetFn` must cover `DeleteSession` + `CreateSession` + `historySrc.Reset()` atomically.
414: - `OnCompact: nil` disables history indexing silently — no hook call, no error.
415: 
416: ### 6. Run the llm-api HTTP server
417: 
418: ```bash
419: # Start — indexes .opencode/skills and listens on :7700
420: go run ./cmd/llm-api/ \
421:     -skills /path/to/.opencode/skills \
422:     -addr   127.0.0.1:7700 \
423:     -llm-url https://api.openai.com/v1 \
424:     -llm-key sk-your-api-key \
425:     -model  gpt-4o
426: 
427: # Health check
428: curl http://127.0.0.1:7700/health
429: # → {"status":"ok","doc_count":3,"session_count":0}
430: 
431: # Search the knowledge index
432: curl "http://127.0.0.1:7700/search?q=context+compaction&max_results=3"
433: 
434: # Chat with SSE streaming (session persists across requests)
435: curl -sN -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7700/chat \
436:     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
437:     -d '{"message":"Explain how context compaction works."}'
438: 
439: # Continue the same session
440: curl -sN -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7700/chat \
441:     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
442:     -d '{"message":"Give me a code example.","session_id":"sess-from-x-session-id-header"}'
443: 
444: # Inspect stored messages
445: curl http://127.0.0.1:7700/sessions/{session-id}/messages
446: ```
447: 
448: **SSE event format:**
449: 
450: ```
451: data: {"type":"text","delta":"Context compaction fires when..."}
452: data: {"type":"tool_call","tool":"knowledge_search","input":{"query":"compaction"}}
453: data: {"type":"tool_result","tool":"knowledge_search","output":"## Result 1\n..."}
454: data: {"type":"done","session_id":"sess-1234567890"}
455: ```

501: 
502: ## Testing
503: 
504: ### Unit tests (no network required)
505: 
506: ```bash
507: go test ./llm/... ./config/... ./session/... ./store/... ./tool/... ./knowledge/...
508: ```
509: 
510: ### Integration tests (requires a live LLM endpoint)
511: 
512: ```bash
513: export LLM_INTEGRATION=1
514: export TIMI_BASE_URL="http://your-llm-proxy/v1"
515: export TIMI_API_KEY="sk-your-key"
516: export TIMI_MODEL="claude-sonnet-4.6"
517: 
518: # Core integration tests
519: go test ./integration/... -v -count=1 -timeout=120s
520: 
521: # Context overflow + compaction end-to-end
522: go test ./integration/overflow/... -v -count=1 -timeout=300s
523: 
524: # Knowledge retrieval + LLM usage
525: go test ./integration/knowledge/... -v -count=1 -timeout=120s
526: ```
527: 
528: ### llm-api feature test (requires running server)
529: 
530: ```bash
531: go run ./cmd/llm-api/ -skills .opencode/skills -addr 127.0.0.1:7700 &
532: 
533: bash cmd/llm-api/test_features.sh
534: # → Passed: 32 / 32 — ALL TESTS PASSED
535: ```
536: 
537: The shell test covers: normal tool call, multi-turn memory, knowledge search/fetch,
538: recoverable tool failure, `max_steps` enforcement, stateful counters, context
539: compaction, async tool execution, all SSE event types, and session inspection.
540: 
541: ---
542: 
543: ## Key Design Decisions
544: 
545: **Provider-agnostic core** — `llm.Provider` is a single interface (`ID()` +
546: `Stream()`). Anthropic and OpenAI adapters translate their native SDK events into
547: the same canonical `llm.Event` stream. New providers implement one interface.
548: 
549: **Immediate turn handoff** — `RunHandle` exposes two channels: `StoreDone`
550: (closed once the current turn's store writes are complete, before Prune) and
551: `Done` (closed after full cleanup including Prune). A new turn can pass
552: `prev.StoreDone` as `RunInput.WaitFor` to start immediately without waiting
553: for Prune, while still guaranteeing a consistent store view. The user message
554: is written *after* `WaitFor` resolves, so a cancelled wait leaves no orphan
555: records.
556: 
557: **Compaction is transparent to the caller** — `RunLoop` detects overflow via
558: `IsOverflow(usage, model)` after every `EventStepFinish`. It calls `Compact()`
559: internally, inserts a summary message into the store, then retries the turn.
560: The caller sees no difference; the session simply continues.
561: 
562: **Tool failure vs. fatal error** — returning `tool.Fail("message")` from a
563: tool produces an error tool-result that the LLM receives and can reason about.
564: The session continues. Any other error stops the session immediately.
565: 
566: **Two-level knowledge retrieval** — `knowledge_search` calls `Source.Peek()`
567: and returns only snippets (minimal context growth). The LLM decides whether to
568: call `knowledge_fetch` with a `ref_id` to retrieve the full document. This keeps
569: the context window small by default.
570: 
571: **RefID routing** — every `Result.RefID` has the form `"{sourceID}:{key}"`.
572: The manager uses `strings.Cut` to route `knowledge_fetch` directly to the correct
573: source in O(1), avoiding a linear scan across all sources.
574: 
575: **SummaryProvider separation** — the compaction summary LLM call uses a separate
576: `SummaryProvider` (when provided). This prevents middleware (e.g., the SSE event
577: forwarder in `llm-api`) from leaking internal summary events to external
578: clients.
579: 
580: ---
581: 
582: ## Requirements
583: 
584: - Go 1.25+
585: - An OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic LLM endpoint
586: - No CGO required for the core library; Bleve's FAISS backend requires CGO if
587:   used (the in-memory Bleve index used by `llm-api` does not)
588: 
589: ---
590: 
591: ## Acknowledgements
592:

595: open-source project [**opencode**](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode).
596: The original TypeScript implementation can be found at
597: `packages/opencode/src/session/` in that repository.

了解，以下是 llm-go 的概览：

## llm-go 项目概览

`llm-go` 是 [opencode](https://github.com/sst/opencode) LLM 层的 Go 移植版本，模块路径为 `github.com/larryhou/llm-go`。

### 核心功能

| 功能 | 说明 |
|------|------|
| **流式客户端** | provider-agnostic `llm.Provider` 接口，带指数退避重试 |
| **双 Provider** | `provider/anthropic` 和 `provider/openai`（兼容所有 OpenAI-compatible 端点） |
| **完整 agentic loop** | `session.RunLoop()` — 用户消息 → LLM 流式输出 → 并行工具执行 → 工具结果回传 → 循环直到 `stop` |
| **Context 压缩** | 接近上下文限制时自动摘要旧轮次，对调用方透明 |
| **Doom-loop 检测** | 同一工具以相同参数连续调用 3 次时停止循环 |
| **知识检索** | `knowledge.Manager` 支持多 `Source` 后端，two-level 检索（先 snippet，再 full doc） |
| **Bleve 全文索引** | `knowledge/source/bleve`，支持内存或磁盘索引 |
| **HTTP API** | `cmd/llm-api` — SSE 流式 chat + REST 搜索端点 |

### 包结构

```
llm/          — 核心类型、错误分类、重试
provider/     — Anthropic / OpenAI 适配器
session/      — RunLoop、compaction、context 转换
tool/         — Tool 接口、Registry、结果截断
store/        — Session/Message/Part CRUD 接口
knowledge/    — Manager、Source 接口、Bleve 实现
config/       — 配置加载
auth/         — auth.json 读写
cmd/          — llm-api HTTP 服务、index-skills CLI
```

### 关键设计决策

- **`RunHandle`** 暴露两个 channel：`StoreDone`（store 写完）和 `Done`（完整清理），支持即时 turn 切换
- **RefID 路由**：`{sourceID}:{key}` 格式，O(1) 定位目标 source
- **`SummaryProvider` 分离**：压缩摘要调用使用独立 provider，避免内部事件泄漏给外部客户端
- **工具失败 vs 致命错误**：`tool.Fail()` 让 LLM 收到错误结果并继续；其他错误立即终止

1: // Package llm defines the Provider interface and core streaming client.
2: package llm
3: 
4: import (
5: 	"context"
6: 	"time"
7: )
8: 
9: // Provider is the abstraction over a specific LLM provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.).
10: // Implementations live in provider/anthropic and provider/openai.
11: type Provider interface {
12: 	// ID returns the provider identifier (e.g. "anthropic", "openai").
13: 	ID() string
14: 
15: 	// Stream sends a request and returns a channel of events.
16: 	// The channel is closed when the stream ends or an error occurs.
17: 	// Callers must drain the channel until it's closed.
18: 	// Cancelling ctx aborts the stream.
19: 	Stream(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan Event, error)
20: }
21: 
22: // Client wraps a Provider and adds retry logic.
23: type Client struct {
24: 	provider   Provider
25: 	maxRetries int
26: }
27: 
28: // NewClient creates a new Client wrapping the given Provider.
29: func NewClient(p Provider) *Client {
30: 	return &Client{provider: p, maxRetries: 5}
31: }
32: 
33: // Stream starts an LLM stream with automatic retry on retryable errors.
34: // Returns a channel of events; closed when the stream finishes or fatally errors.
35: func (c *Client) Stream(ctx context.Context, req Request) <-chan Event {
36: 	ch := make(chan Event, 32)
37: 	go func() {
38: 		defer close(ch)
39: 		c.streamWithRetry(ctx, req, ch)
40: 	}()
41: 	return ch
42: }
43: 
44: func (c *Client) streamWithRetry(ctx context.Context, req Request, out chan<- Event) {
45: 	for attempt := 1; attempt <= c.maxRetries; attempt++ {
46: 		retry, done := c.doStream(ctx, req, out, attempt)
47: 		if done {
48: 			return
49: 		}
50: 		if !retry {
51: 			return
52: 		}
53: 		// retry — caller provided a delay already via retryErr.ResponseHeaders
54: 	}
55: }
56: 
57: // doStream runs one streaming attempt.
58: // Returns (shouldRetry, isDone).
59: func (c *Client) doStream(ctx context.Context, req Request, out chan<- Event, attempt int) (bool, bool) {
60: 	events, err := c.provider.Stream(ctx, req)
61: 	if err != nil {
62: 		if llmErr, ok := AsLLMError(err); ok && ShouldRetry(llmErr) && attempt < c.maxRetries {
63: 			if !c.sleep(ctx, RetryDelay(attempt, llmErr.ResponseHeaders)) {
64: 				out <- Event{Type: EventError, Err: ctx.Err()}
65: 				return false, true
66: 			}
67: 			return true, false
68: 		}
69: 		out <- Event{Type: EventError, Err: err}
70: 		return false, true
71: 	}
72: 
73: 	// Buffer all events from this attempt; only flush to out once we receive
74: 	// EventRequestFinish. On retry, discard the buffer so the caller never
75: 	// sees a partial sequence from a failed attempt.
76: 	var buf []Event
77: 	var retryErr *LLMError
78: 	for ev := range events {
79: 		if ev.Type == EventError {
80: 			if llmErr, ok := AsLLMError(ev.Err); ok && ShouldRetry(llmErr) && attempt < c.maxRetries {
81: 				retryErr = llmErr
82: 				// drain remaining events from provider
83: 				for range events {
84: 				}
85: 				break
86: 			}
87: 			// Fatal error — flush buffer then send error so caller gets context.
88: 			for _, buffered := range buf {
89: 				out <- buffered
90: 			}
91: 			out <- ev
92: 			return false, true
93: 		}
94: 		buf = append(buf, ev)
95: 		if ev.Type == EventRequestFinish {
96: 			for _, buffered := range buf {
97: 				out <- buffered
98: 			}
99: 			return false, true
100: 		}
101: 	}
102: 
103: 	if retryErr != nil {
104: 		if !c.sleep(ctx, RetryDelay(attempt, retryErr.ResponseHeaders)) {
105: 			out <- Event{Type: EventError, Err: ctx.Err()}
106: 			return false, true
107: 		}
108: 		return true, false
109: 	}
110: 	return false, true
111: }
112: 
113: // sleep waits for d or until ctx is cancelled. Returns false if ctx was cancelled.
114: func (c *Client) sleep(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) bool {
115: 	select {
116: 	case <-ctx.Done():
117: 		return false
118: 	case <-time.After(d):
119: 		return true
120: 	}
121: }

1: package llm
2: 
3: import (
4: 	"errors"

7: 	"regexp"

10: 	"time"
11: )
12: 
13: // ErrorKind classifies LLM errors for retry/reporting decisions.
14: // Aligned with packages/llm/src/schema/errors.ts ErrorReason.
15: type ErrorKind string
16: 
17: const (
18: 	ErrContextOverflow  ErrorKind = "context_overflow"
19: 	ErrAuth             ErrorKind = "auth"
20: 	ErrRateLimit        ErrorKind = "rate_limit"
21: 	ErrQuotaExceeded    ErrorKind = "quota_exceeded"
22: 	ErrInvalidRequest   ErrorKind = "invalid_request"
23: 	ErrContentPolicy    ErrorKind = "content_policy"
24: 	ErrProviderInternal ErrorKind = "provider_internal"
25: 	ErrTransport        ErrorKind = "transport"
26: 	ErrUnknown          ErrorKind = "unknown"
27: )
28: 
29: // LLMError is the canonical error type returned by LLM operations.
30: type LLMError struct {
31: 	Kind            ErrorKind
32: 	Message         string
33: 	StatusCode      int
34: 	IsRetryable     bool
35: 	ResponseBody    string
36: 	ResponseHeaders http.Header
37: }
38: 
39: func (e *LLMError) Error() string {
40: 	if e.StatusCode != 0 {
41: 		return fmt.Sprintf("llm error [%s] status=%d: %s", e.Kind, e.StatusCode, e.Message)
42: 	}
43: 	return fmt.Sprintf("llm error [%s]: %s", e.Kind, e.Message)
44: }
45: 
46: // IsContextOverflow returns true if this error indicates the context window was exceeded.
47: func (e *LLMError) IsContextOverflow() bool { return e.Kind == ErrContextOverflow }
48: 
49: // AsLLMError extracts an *LLMError from an error chain.
50: func AsLLMError(err error) (*LLMError, bool) {
51: 	var e *LLMError
52: 	return e, errors.As(err, &e)
53: }
54: 
55: // overflowPatterns is the canonical list of 17+ patterns indicating context overflow.
56: // Aligned with packages/opencode/src/provider/error.ts OVERFLOW_PATTERNS.
57: var overflowPatterns = []*regexp.Regexp{
58: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)prompt is too long`),                                    // Anthropic
59: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)input is too long for requested model`),                 // Bedrock
60: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)exceeds the context window`),                            // OpenAI
61: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)input token count.*exceeds the maximum`),                // Google Gemini
62: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)maximum prompt length is \d+`),                         // xAI Grok
63: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)reduce the length of the messages`),                     // Groq
64: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)maximum context length is \d+ tokens`),                 // OpenRouter/DeepSeek/vLLM
65: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)exceeds the limit of \d+`),                             // GitHub Copilot
66: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)exceeds the available context size`),                   // llama.cpp
67: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)greater than the context length`),                      // LM Studio
68: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)context window exceeds limit`),                         // MiniMax
69: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)exceeded model token limit`),                           // Kimi/Moonshot
70: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)context[_ ]length[_ ]exceeded`),                       // Generic
71: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)request entity too large`),                             // HTTP 413
72: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)context length is only \d+ tokens`),                   // vLLM
73: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)input length.*exceeds.*context length`),                // vLLM
74: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)prompt too long; exceeded (?:max )?context length`),   // Ollama
75: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)too large for model with \d+ maximum context length`), // Mistral
76: 	regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)model_context_window_exceeded`),                       // z.ai
77: }
78: 
79: // emptyBodyPattern matches Cerebras/Mistral "400 (no body)" style errors.
80: var emptyBodyPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)^4(00|13)\s*(status code)?\s*\(no body\)`)
81: 
82: // isOverflowMessage returns true if the message indicates a context overflow.
83: func isOverflowMessage(msg string) bool {
84: 	for _, p := range overflowPatterns {
85: 		if p.MatchString(msg) {
86: 			return true
87: 		}
88: 	}
89: 	return emptyBodyPattern.MatchString(msg)
90: }
91: 
92: // ClassifyHTTPError converts an HTTP status code + response body into an LLMError.
93: // Aligned with packages/opencode/src/provider/error.ts parseAPICallError.
94: func ClassifyHTTPError(providerID string, statusCode int, body string, headers http.Header) *LLMError {
95: 	msg := extractMessage(providerID, statusCode, body)
96: 
97: 	// Check for context overflow first
98: 	if isOverflowMessage(msg) || statusCode == 413 || isBodyContextOverflow(body) {
99: 		return &LLMError{
100: 			Kind:         ErrContextOverflow,
101: 			Message:      msg,
102: 			StatusCode:   statusCode,
103: 			IsRetryable:  false,
104: 			ResponseBody: body,
105: 		}
106: 	}
107: 
108: 	kind, retryable := classifyStatus(statusCode, body)
109: 	return &LLMError{
110: 		Kind:            kind,
111: 		Message:         msg,
112: 		StatusCode:      statusCode,
113: 		IsRetryable:     retryable,
114: 		ResponseBody:    body,
115: 		ResponseHeaders: headers,
116: 	}
117: }
118: 
119: // ClassifyStreamError parses JSON error events from the stream.
120: // Aligned with packages/opencode/src/provider/error.ts parseStreamError.
121: func ClassifyStreamError(errorType, errorCode, message string) *LLMError {
122: 	switch {
123: 	case errorCode == "context_length_exceeded" || errorType == "context_length_exceeded":
124: 		return &LLMError{Kind: ErrContextOverflow, Message: message, IsRetryable: false}
125: 	case errorCode == "insufficient_quota":
126: 		return &LLMError{Kind: ErrQuotaExceeded, Message: message, IsRetryable: false}
127: 	case errorCode == "usage_not_included" || errorCode == "invalid_prompt":
128: 		return &LLMError{Kind: ErrInvalidRequest, Message: message, IsRetryable: false}
129: 	case errorCode == "server_is_overloaded" || errorType == "server_error":
130: 		return &LLMError{Kind: ErrProviderInternal, Message: message, IsRetryable: true}
131: 	}
132: 	return nil
133: }
134: 
135: // classifyStatus maps HTTP status codes to ErrorKind + retryable flag.
136: func classifyStatus(statusCode int, body string) (ErrorKind, bool) {
137: 	switch {
138: 	case statusCode == 401 || statusCode == 403:
139: 		return ErrAuth, false
140: 	case statusCode == 429:
141: 		// Distinguish rate limit vs quota exceeded via body keywords
142: 		b := strings.ToLower(body)
143: 		if strings.Contains(b, "quota") || strings.Contains(b, "billing") {
144: 			return ErrQuotaExceeded, false
145: 		}
146: 		return ErrRateLimit, true
147: 	case statusCode == 400 || statusCode == 404 || statusCode == 422:
148: 		return ErrInvalidRequest, false
149: 	case statusCode == 529: // Anthropic overloaded — must precede >= 500
150: 		return ErrProviderInternal, true
151: 	case statusCode >= 500:
152: 		return ErrProviderInternal, true
153: 	}
154: 	return ErrUnknown, false
155: }
156: 
157: // isBodyContextOverflow checks JSON body for context_length_exceeded code.
158: func isBodyContextOverflow(body string) bool {
159: 	// fast string check before full parse
160: 	return strings.Contains(body, "context_length_exceeded")
161: }
162: 
163: // extractMessage builds a human-readable error message from the response.
164: // Aligned with packages/opencode/src/provider/error.ts message().
165: func extractMessage(providerID string, statusCode int, body string) string {
166: 	if body == "" {
167: 		return httpStatusText(statusCode)
168: 	}
169: 	// Reject HTML bodies (gateway error pages)
170: 	trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(body)
171: 	if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "<!") || strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "<html") {
172: 		switch statusCode {
173: 		case 401:
174: 			return "Unauthorized: check your API key"
175: 		case 403:
176: 			return "Forbidden: insufficient permissions"
177: 		default:
178: 			return fmt.Sprintf("HTTP %d from %s", statusCode, providerID)
179: 		}
180: 	}
181: 	return body
182: }
183: 
184: func httpStatusText(code int) string {
185: 	if t := http.StatusText(code); t != "" {
186: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%d %s", code, t)
187: 	}
188: 	return fmt.Sprintf("HTTP %d", code)
189: }
190: 
191: // RetryDelay calculates the delay before the next retry attempt.
192: // Aligned with packages/opencode/src/session/retry.ts delay().
193: //
194: // Priority:
195: //  1. retry-after-ms header (ms float)
196: //  2. retry-after header (seconds float or HTTP date)
197: //  3. Exponential backoff: 2000ms × 2^(attempt-1), capped at 30s
198: func RetryDelay(attempt int, headers http.Header) time.Duration {
199: 	if headers != nil {
200: 		if v := headers.Get("retry-after-ms"); v != "" {
201: 			if ms, err := strconv.ParseFloat(v, 64); err == nil && ms > 0 {
202: 				return time.Duration(ms) * time.Millisecond
203: 			}
204: 		}
205: 		if v := headers.Get("retry-after"); v != "" {
206: 			// Try as seconds
207: 			if secs, err := strconv.ParseFloat(v, 64); err == nil && secs > 0 {
208: 				return time.Duration(secs*1000) * time.Millisecond
209: 			}
210: 			// Try as HTTP date

224: 	)
225: 	delay := initial
226: 	for i := 1; i < attempt; i++ {
227: 		delay *= 2
228: 		if delay > maxDelay {
229: 			return maxDelay
230: 		}
231: 	}
232: 	return delay
233: }

1: // Package llm provides RecordProvider — a stateless transparent wrapper
2: // that appends one JSON record per Stream() call to a recording file.
3: //
4: // # Format
5: //
6: // The recording file is newline-delimited JSON (ndjson). Each line is one
7: // Record — the full request plus the filtered response events:
8: //
9: //	{"request":{...},"events":[{"type":"request-start"},{"type":"step-start"},{"type":"text-delta","text":"..."},{"type":"step-finish","finish_reason":"stop","usage":{"input":1234,"output":56}},{"type":"request-finish","finish_reason":"stop"}]}
10: //	{"request":{...},"events":[...]}
11: //
12: // One file covers the entire session lifetime. The replay provider reads the
13: // file and consumes one line per Stream() call, in order.
14: //
15: // Only semantically significant events are stored. Low-level lifecycle events
16: // (TextStart/End, ToolInputStart/Delta) are synthesised by the replay provider.
17: // EventStepFinish.Usage carries real token counts — critical for compaction.
18: package llm
19: 
20: import (
21: 	"context"
22: 	"encoding/json"
23: 	"fmt"
24: 	"os"
25: 	"sync"
26: )
27: 
28: // ── Types ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
29: 
30: // RecordEvent is a JSON-serialisable snapshot of one llm.Event.
31: type RecordEvent struct {
32: 	Type         EventType    `json:"type"`
33: 	Text         string       `json:"text,omitempty"`
34: 	Signature    string       `json:"signature,omitempty"`
35: 	ToolCallID   string       `json:"tool_call_id,omitempty"`
36: 	ToolName     string       `json:"tool_name,omitempty"`
37: 	Input        any          `json:"input,omitempty"`
38: 	FinishReason FinishReason `json:"finish_reason,omitempty"`
39: 	Usage        *TokenUsage  `json:"usage,omitempty"`
40: 	Error        string       `json:"error,omitempty"`
41: }
42: 
43: // Record is one line in the recording file: the request sent to the LLM
44: // and the significant response events.
45: type Record struct {
46: 	Request Request         `json:"request"`
47: 	Events  []RecordEvent `json:"events"`
48: }
49: 
50: // ── RecordProvider ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
51: 
52: // RecordProvider wraps a real Provider and appends one Record per
53: // Stream() call to path. It is fully transparent — no lifecycle methods, no
54: // turn-boundary logic. The file can be replayed with DebugProvider.
55: type RecordProvider struct {
56: 	inner Provider
57: 	mu    sync.Mutex
58: 	f     *os.File
59: 	enc   *json.Encoder
60: }
61: 
62: // NewRecordProvider wraps inner and records every Stream() call to path.
63: // The file is created (or truncated) immediately; an error is returned if it
64: // cannot be opened.
65: func NewRecordProvider(inner Provider, path string) (*RecordProvider, error) {
66: 	f, err := os.Create(path)
67: 	if err != nil {
68: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("recording: create %s: %w", path, err)
69: 	}
70: 	enc := json.NewEncoder(f)
71: 	enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
72: 	return &RecordProvider{inner: inner, f: f, enc: enc}, nil
73: }
74: 
75: // ID satisfies llm.Provider.
76: func (p *RecordProvider) ID() string { return p.inner.ID() }
77: 
78: // Close flushes and closes the recording file.
79: func (p *RecordProvider) Close() error {
80: 	p.mu.Lock()
81: 	defer p.mu.Unlock()
82: 	return p.f.Close()
83: }
84: 
85: // Stream satisfies llm.Provider. It transparently proxies to the inner
86: // provider while recording the request and all significant response events.
87: // One Record is appended to the file when the stream closes.
88: func (p *RecordProvider) Stream(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan Event, error) {
89: 	inner, err := p.inner.Stream(ctx, req)
90: 	if err != nil {
91: 		return nil, err
92: 	}
93: 
94: 	out := make(chan Event, 128)
95: 	go func() {
96: 		defer close(out)
97: 
98: 		step := Record{
99: 			Request: req,
100: 			Events:  []RecordEvent{{Type: EventRequestStart}},
101: 		}
102: 
103: 		for ev := range inner {
104: 			select {
105: 			case out <- ev:
106: 			case <-ctx.Done():
107: 				for range inner {
108: 				}
109: 				return
110: 			}
111: 			recordEvent(&step, ev)
112: 		}
113: 
114: 		p.mu.Lock()
115: 		_ = p.enc.Encode(step)
116: 		p.mu.Unlock()
117: 	}()
118: 
119: 	return out, nil
120: }
121: 
122: // recordEvent appends significant events to step, accumulating text/reasoning
123: // deltas into a single record per LLM step.
124: func recordEvent(step *Record, ev Event) {
125: 	switch ev.Type {
126: 	case EventStepStart:
127: 		step.Events = append(step.Events, RecordEvent{Type: EventStepStart})
128: 
129: 	case EventTextDelta:
130: 		accumulateDelta(step, EventTextDelta, ev.Text)
131: 
132: 	case EventReasoningDelta:
133: 		accumulateDelta(step, EventReasoningDelta, ev.Text)
134: 
135: 	case EventReasoningEnd:
136: 		step.Events = append(step.Events, RecordEvent{Type: EventReasoningEnd, Signature: ev.Signature})
137: 
138: 	case EventToolCall:
139: 		step.Events = append(step.Events, RecordEvent{
140: 			Type:       EventToolCall,
141: 			ToolName:   ev.ToolName,
142: 			ToolCallID: ev.ToolCallID,
143: 			Input:      ev.Input,
144: 		})
145: 
146: 	case EventStepFinish:
147: 		u := ev.Usage
148: 		step.Events = append(step.Events, RecordEvent{
149: 			Type:         EventStepFinish,
150: 			FinishReason: ev.FinishReason,
151: 			Usage:        &u,
152: 		})
153: 
154: 	case EventRequestFinish:
155: 		step.Events = append(step.Events, RecordEvent{
156: 			Type:         EventRequestFinish,
157: 			FinishReason: ev.FinishReason,
158: 		})
159: 
160: 	case EventError:
161: 		errStr := ""
162: 		if ev.Err != nil {
163: 			errStr = ev.Err.Error()
164: 		}
165: 		step.Events = append(step.Events, RecordEvent{Type: EventError, Error: errStr})
166: 	}
167: }
168: 
169: // accumulateDelta merges a text delta into the last matching RecordEvent within
170: // the current LLM step, or appends a new one if none exists yet.
171: func accumulateDelta(step *Record, t EventType, text string) {
172: 	for i := len(step.Events) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
173: 		if step.Events[i].Type == EventStepStart {
174: 			break
175: 		}
176: 		if step.Events[i].Type == t {
177: 			step.Events[i].Text += text
178: 			return
179: 		}
180: 	}
181: 	step.Events = append(step.Events, RecordEvent{Type: t, Text: text})
182: }

1: // Package llm provides ReplayProvider — a replay provider that drives a session
2: // from a recording file produced by RecordingProvider.
3: //
4: // Each Stream() call consumes the next Record from the file and synthesises
5: // the recorded events as a live event stream, including real token usage.
6: // The provider is stateless beyond the read cursor; it knows nothing about
7: // turns or sessions.
8: package llm
9: 
10: import (
11: 	"bufio"
12: 	"context"
13: 	"encoding/json"
14: 	"errors"
15: 	"fmt"
16: 	"io"
17: 	"os"
18: 	"sync/atomic"
19: )
20: 
21: // ReplayProvider replays a sequence of Records as live event streams.
22: // Each call to Stream() consumes the next Record in order.
23: // Construct with NewReplayProvider (from file) or NewReplayProviderFromRecords (from slice).
24: type ReplayProvider struct {
25: 	steps []Record
26: 	idx   atomic.Int64
27: }
28: 
29: // NewReplayProvider loads all Records from the ndjson recording at path.
30: func NewReplayProvider(path string) (*ReplayProvider, error) {
31: 	f, err := os.Open(path)
32: 	if err != nil {
33: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("replay provider: open %s: %w", path, err)
34: 	}
35: 	defer f.Close()
36: 
37: 	var steps []Record
38: 	dec := json.NewDecoder(bufio.NewReader(f))
39: 	for {
40: 		var s Record
41: 		if err := dec.Decode(&s); errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
42: 			break
43: 		} else if err != nil {
44: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("replay provider: decode %s: %w", path, err)
45: 		}
46: 		steps = append(steps, s)
47: 	}
48: 	if len(steps) == 0 {
49: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("replay provider: %s has no steps", path)
50: 	}
51: 	return &ReplayProvider{steps: steps}, nil
52: }
53: 
54: // NewReplayProviderFromRecords creates a ReplayProvider from an in-memory slice.
55: func NewReplayProviderFromRecords(records []Record) *ReplayProvider {
56: 	return &ReplayProvider{steps: records}
57: }
58: 
59: // ID satisfies llm.Provider.
60: func (p *ReplayProvider) ID() string { return "replay" }
61: 
62: // Len returns the total number of recorded steps.
63: func (p *ReplayProvider) Len() int { return len(p.steps) }
64: 
65: // Records returns a copy of the underlying Record slice.
66: // Used by cmd/replay to group steps into turns without re-parsing the file.
67: func (p *ReplayProvider) Records() []Record { return p.steps }
68: 
69: // Stream satisfies llm.Provider. It replays the next recorded Record as a
70: // live event stream, synthesising low-level lifecycle events from the stored
71: // higher-level ones so that session.Processor behaves identically to a real run.
72: func (p *ReplayProvider) Stream(_ context.Context, _ Request) (<-chan Event, error) {
73: 	i := int(p.idx.Add(1) - 1)
74: 	if i >= len(p.steps) {
75: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("replay provider: no more steps (have %d, attempted step %d)", len(p.steps), i+1)
76: 	}
77: 	step := p.steps[i]
78: 
79: 	ch := make(chan Event, 256)
80: 	go func() {
81: 		defer close(ch)
82: 		for _, re := range step.Events {
83: 			for _, ev := range expand(re) {
84: 				ch <- ev
85: 			}
86: 		}
87: 	}()
88: 	return ch, nil
89: }
90: 
91: // expand converts one RecordEvent back into the sequence of live Events that
92: // session.Processor expects. Low-level lifecycle events that were omitted
93: // during recording are re-synthesised here.
94: func expand(re RecordEvent) []Event {
95: 	switch re.Type {
96: 	case EventRequestStart:
97: 		return []Event{{Type: EventRequestStart}}
98: 
99: 	case EventStepStart:
100: 		return []Event{{Type: EventStepStart}}
101: 
102: 	case EventTextDelta:
103: 		return []Event{
104: 			{Type: EventTextStart},
105: 			{Type: EventTextDelta, Text: re.Text},
106: 			{Type: EventTextEnd},
107: 		}
108: 
109: 	case EventReasoningDelta:
110: 		return []Event{
111: 			{Type: EventReasoningDelta, Text: re.Text},
112: 			{Type: EventReasoningEnd, Signature: re.Signature},
113: 		}
114: 
115: 	case EventReasoningEnd:
116: 		// Already emitted by EventReasoningDelta expansion; skip standalone.
117: 		return nil
118: 
119: 	case EventToolCall:
120: 		return []Event{
121: 			{Type: EventToolInputStart, ToolName: re.ToolName, ToolCallID: re.ToolCallID},
122: 			{Type: EventToolCall, ToolName: re.ToolName, ToolCallID: re.ToolCallID, Input: re.Input},
123: 		}
124: 
125: 	case EventStepFinish:
126: 		usage := TokenUsage{}
127: 		if re.Usage != nil {
128: 			usage = *re.Usage
129: 		}
130: 		return []Event{{Type: EventStepFinish, FinishReason: re.FinishReason, Usage: usage}}
131: 
132: 	case EventRequestFinish:
133: 		return []Event{{Type: EventRequestFinish, FinishReason: re.FinishReason}}
134: 
135: 	case EventError:
136: 		return []Event{{Type: EventError, Err: errors.New(re.Error)}}
137: 	}
138: 	return nil
139: }

以下是对 `llm` 包的详细分析：

---

## llm 包详细分析

`llm` 包是整个项目的**核心基础层**，定义了所有上层代码共用的规范类型、接口和算法。共 8 个文件。

---

### 1. `message.go` — 会话消息类型

**核心数据模型**，对齐 opencode TypeScript 版的 `schema/messages.ts`。

```
Message
  └── Role: user | assistant | tool | system
  └── Content: []ContentPart
        ├── text          → Text
        ├── reasoning     → Text + Signature (Anthropic thinking block，必须原样回传)
        ├── tool-call     → ToolCallID + ToolName + Input
        ├── tool-result   → ToolCallID + ToolName + Result(*ToolResult)
        ├── image         → MediaType + Data/URL
        └── file          → MediaType + Data/URL
```

**`ToolResult`** 是三态枚举：
- `json` — 结构化输出，Value 为 `any`
- `text` — 纯文本
- `error` — 工具执行失败（LLM 可感知并推理）

**`Request`** 是发给 provider 的完整请求：
- `Model` — 模型标识 + 限制
- `System []string` — 系统提示（多段）
- `Messages []Message` — 对话历史
- `Tools []ToolDefinition` — 工具 schema 列表
- `ToolChoice` — `auto | none | required | <name>`
- `Options` — MaxTokens / Temperature / TopP / TopK

**`TokenUsage`** 追踪 token 消耗，`Effective()` 优先使用 `Total` 字段，`Total=0` 时累加所有分项——与 OpenAI 直接报 total、Anthropic 分项报告的差异兼容。

---

### 2. `event.go` — 流式事件系统

完整的事件生命周期（13 种类型）：

```
EventRequestStart
  └── EventStepStart            ← 每次 LLM 调用开始
        ├── EventTextStart
        │     EventTextDelta    ← 文本流式增量
        │     EventTextEnd
        ├── EventReasoningDelta ← 推理（thinking）增量
        │   EventReasoningEnd   ← 携带 Signature
        ├── EventToolInputStart
        │   EventToolInputDelta ← 工具参数流式增量
        │   EventToolCall       ← 完整工具调用（含解析后 Input）
        │   EventToolResult     ← 工具执行结果
        │   EventToolError      ← 工具执行失败
        └── EventStepFinish     ← 携带 Usage + FinishReason
EventRequestFinish              ← 整个请求结束
EventError                      ← 携带 Err
```

`FinishReason`: `stop | tool-calls | length | error | other`

`Event` 是**扁平 struct**，用 `Type` 字段区分有效字段，避免 interface{} 带来的分配开销。

---

### 3. `client.go` — 带重试的流式客户端

```
Provider (interface)
  ├── ID() string
  └── Stream(ctx, req) (<-chan Event, error)

Client
  └── maxRetries: 5
  └── Stream() → goroutine → streamWithRetry()
```

**重试策略的精妙设计**：

```
doStream():
  1. 调用 provider.Stream() 
  2. 将所有事件 buffer 到 []Event
  3. 收到 EventRequestFinish → 一次性 flush 到 out channel
  4. 中途收到可重试 error → 丢弃 buffer，sleep，重试
  5. 致命 error → flush 已有 buffer（让调用方获得上下文）再发 error
```

关键设计：**mid-stream 重试时调用方看不到半截序列**，只有完整成功的流或最终错误。

`sleep()` 响应 `ctx.Done()`，cancel 时立即退出而不等待 sleep 结束。

---

### 4. `error.go` — 错误分类系统

**`ErrorKind`** 枚举（8 种）：

| Kind | 可重试 | 场景 |
|------|--------|------|
| `context_overflow` | 否 | 上下文超限 |
| `auth` | 否 | 401/403 |
| `rate_limit` | 是 | 429（非quota） |
| `quota_exceeded` | 否 | 429（含quota/billing关键字） |
| `invalid_request` | 否 | 400/404/422 |
| `content_policy` | 否 | 内容审查 |
| `provider_internal` | 是 | 5xx / 529 |
| `transport` | — | 网络层错误 |

**`overflowPatterns`** — 19 个正则，覆盖主流 provider 的上下文超限错误消息（Anthropic/Bedrock/OpenAI/Gemini/Grok/Groq/OpenRouter/vLLM/llama.cpp/LM Studio 等）。

**`RetryDelay`** — 三级优先：
1. `Retry-After-Ms` header（毫秒）
2. `Retry-After` header（秒 或 HTTP date）
3. 指数退避：`2s → 4s → 8s → 16s → 30s`（上限 30s）

---

### 5. `overflow.go` — 上下文溢出数学

**`Usable(model, cfg)`** — 计算可用 token 上限：
```
if model.limit.input != nil:
    usable = input_limit - reserved
else:
    usable = context - maxOutputTokens(model)

reserved = cfg.compaction.reserved ?? min(20_000, maxOutputTokens)
```

**`IsOverflow(usage, model, cfg)`**：
- `compaction.auto=false` 时永不触发
- `usage.Effective() >= Usable()` 时返回 true

**`PreserveRecentBudget()`** — 计算压缩时保留最近轮次的 token 预算：
```
cfg.preserve_recent_tokens ?? clamp(floor(usable * 0.25), 2_000, 8_000)
```

常量对齐 opencode 原版：
- `CompactionBuffer = 20_000`
- `MinPreserveRecentTokens = 2_000`
- `MaxPreserveRecentTokens = 8_000`

---

### 6. `record_provider.go` — 会话录制

`RecordProvider` 是 `Provider` 的**透明包装**，将每次 `Stream()` 调用录制为 ndjson 文件中的一行：

```json
{"request":{...},"events":[{"type":"step-start"},{"type":"text-delta","text":"..."},{"type":"step-finish","finish_reason":"stop","usage":{...}}]}
```

**存储优化**：
- 只存语义显著的事件（`TextStart/End`、`ToolInputDelta` 等低层事件**不存储**）
- `accumulateDelta()` 将同一 step 内的文本增量**合并**为单条记录
- 每次 Stream() 结束时一次性写入（`sync.Mutex` 保护并发写）

---

### 7. `replay_provider.go` — 会话回放

`ReplayProvider` 从录制文件重建完整的事件流，用于**测试/调试**：

```
NewReplayProvider(path) → 加载全部 Record
Stream() → atomic idx++ → expand(RecordEvent) → []Event
```

**`expand()`** 从紧凑记录反向合成低层事件：
```
RecordEvent{TextDelta}  → [TextStart, TextDelta, TextEnd]
RecordEvent{ToolCall}   → [ToolInputStart, ToolCall]
RecordEvent{Reasoning}  → [ReasoningDelta, ReasoningEnd]
```

`atomic.Int64` 保证并发安全，支持多 goroutine 同时调用 `Stream()`（虽然实际场景是串行的）。

---

### 架构关系总结

```
                    ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                    │         llm 包               │
                    │                              │
  Provider ◄────── Client ──► streamWithRetry     │
     │                              │              │
     ├── anthropic.Provider         │ retry/backoff│
     ├── openai.Provider            │ error.go     │
     ├── RecordProvider ────────────┤              │
     └── ReplayProvider             │              │
                    │               │              │
              message.go        overflow.go        │
              event.go          (IsOverflow,       │
              (types only)       Usable,           │
                                 PreserveRecent)   │
                    └─────────────────────────────┘
                              ▲
                    session/, provider/ 依赖此包
```

`llm` 包**零依赖**上层包（只依赖 `config`），是整个系统的稳定基础层。

77: // Process runs one LLM streaming turn for an assistant message.
78: // It creates the assistant message in the store, streams events from the
79: // provider, executes tool calls, and persists all parts.
80: // Returns the ProcessResult indicating whether to continue, stop, or compact.
81: func (p *Processor) Process(ctx context.Context, assistantMsgID string, input ProcessInput) (ProcessResult, error) {
82: 	// Build the LLM request
83: 	req := llm.Request{
84: 		Model:    input.Model,
85: 		System:   input.System,
86: 		Messages: input.Messages,
87: 		Options:  llm.GenerationOptions{},
88: 	}
89: 
90: 	// Add tool definitions to request
91: 	for _, t := range input.Tools {
92: 		req.Tools = append(req.Tools, llm.ToolDefinition{
93: 			Name:        t.Name(),
94: 			Description: t.Description(),
95: 			InputSchema: t.InputSchema(),
96: 		})
97: 	}
98: 
99: 	// Build tool lookup map
100: 	toolMap := make(map[string]tool.Tool, len(input.Tools))
101: 	for _, t := range input.Tools {
102: 		toolMap[t.Name()] = t
103: 	}
104: 
105: 	client := llm.NewClient(input.Provider)
106: 	events := client.Stream(ctx, req)
107: 
108: 	toolCtx, toolCancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
109: 	state := &processorState{
110: 		store:          p.store,
111: 		sessionID:      input.SessionID,
112: 		assistantMsgID: assistantMsgID,
113: 		toolMap:        toolMap,
114: 		cfg:            input.Config,
115: 		model:          input.Model,
116: 		toolCtx:        toolCtx,
117: 		toolCancel:     toolCancel,
118: 		// recentCalls shared from Processor so doom-loop detection spans steps
119: 		sharedRecentCalls:   &p.recentCalls,
120: 		sharedRecentCallsMu: &p.recentCallsMu,
121: 	}
122: 
123: 	result := ProcessContinue
124: 	for ev := range events {
125: 		r, err := state.handleEvent(ctx, ev)
126: 		if err != nil {
127: 			state.cleanup()
128: 			return ProcessStop, err
129: 		}
130: 		if r != ProcessContinue {
131: 			result = r
132: 			// drain remaining events
133: 			for range events {
134: 			}
135: 			break
136: 		}
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	state.cleanup()
140: 	return result, nil
141: }

192: func (s *processorState) handleEvent(ctx context.Context, ev llm.Event) (ProcessResult, error) {
193: 	switch ev.Type {
194: 	case llm.EventError:
195: 		if llmErr, ok := llm.AsLLMError(ev.Err); ok && llmErr.IsContextOverflow() {
196: 			s.needsCompaction = true
197: 			return ProcessCompact, nil
198: 		}
199: 		return ProcessStop, ev.Err
200: 
201: 	case llm.EventTextStart:
202: 		s.currentTextStart = nowMS()
203: 		s.currentTextBuf = ""
204: 		id, err := s.createPart(ctx, store.PartTypeText, &store.TextPartData{
205: 			TimeStart: s.currentTextStart,
206: 		})
207: 		if err != nil {
208: 			return ProcessStop, err
209: 		}
210: 		s.currentTextPartID = id
211: 
212: 	case llm.EventTextDelta:
213: 		s.currentTextBuf += ev.Text
214: 		if s.currentTextPartID != "" {
215: 			_ = s.updateTextPart(ctx, s.currentTextPartID, s.currentTextBuf, s.currentTextStart, 0)
216: 		}
217: 
218: 	case llm.EventTextEnd:
219: 		if s.currentTextPartID != "" {
220: 			end := nowMS()
221: 			_ = s.updateTextPart(ctx, s.currentTextPartID, s.currentTextBuf, s.currentTextStart, end)
222: 			s.currentTextPartID = ""
223: 			s.currentTextBuf = ""
224: 		}
225: 
226: 	case llm.EventReasoningDelta:
227: 		if s.currentReasoningPartID == "" {
228: 			s.currentReasoningStart = nowMS()
229: 			id, err := s.createPart(ctx, store.PartTypeReasoning, &store.ReasoningPartData{
230: 				TimeStart: s.currentReasoningStart,
231: 			})
232: 			if err != nil {
233: 				return ProcessStop, err
234: 			}
235: 			s.currentReasoningPartID = id
236: 		}
237: 		s.currentReasoningBuf += ev.Text
238: 		_ = s.updateReasoningPart(ctx, s.currentReasoningPartID, s.currentReasoningBuf, s.currentReasoningSignature, s.currentReasoningStart, 0)
239: 
240: 	case llm.EventReasoningEnd:
241: 		if s.currentReasoningPartID != "" {
242: 			s.currentReasoningSignature = ev.Signature
243: 			end := nowMS()
244: 			_ = s.updateReasoningPart(ctx, s.currentReasoningPartID, s.currentReasoningBuf, ev.Signature, s.currentReasoningStart, end)
245: 			s.currentReasoningPartID = ""
246: 			s.currentReasoningBuf = ""
247: 			s.currentReasoningSignature = ""
248: 		}
249: 
250: 	case llm.EventToolInputStart:
251: 		if s.activeToolParts == nil {
252: 			s.activeToolParts = make(map[string]string)
253: 		}
254: 		id, err := s.createPart(ctx, store.PartTypeTool, &store.ToolPartData{
255: 			Tool:      ev.ToolName,
256: 			CallID:    ev.ToolCallID,
257: 			Status:    store.ToolStatusPending,
258: 			TimeStart: nowMS(),
259: 		})
260: 		if err != nil {
261: 			return ProcessStop, err
262: 		}
263: 		s.toolMu.Lock()
264: 		s.activeToolParts[ev.ToolCallID] = id
265: 		s.toolMu.Unlock()
266: 
267: 	case llm.EventToolCall:
268: 		s.toolMu.Lock()
269: 		partID, ok := s.activeToolParts[ev.ToolCallID]
270: 		s.toolMu.Unlock()
271: 		if !ok {
272: 			break
273: 		}
274: 		inputKey := marshalInput(ev.Input)
275: 
276: 		// Doom-loop detection: same tool + same args 3 times in a row
277: 		if s.checkDoomLoop(ev.ToolName, inputKey) {
278: 			// Mark as error and stop
279: 			_ = s.updateToolStatus(ctx, partID, store.ToolStatusError, nil, "Doom loop detected: repeated identical tool call")
280: 			return ProcessStop, fmt.Errorf("doom loop detected for tool %q", ev.ToolName)
281: 		}
282: 
283: 		inputMap := toInputMap(ev.Input)
284: 		_ = s.updateToolRunning(ctx, partID, ev.ToolName, ev.ToolCallID, inputMap)
285: 
286: 		// Execute the tool in a goroutine tracked by toolWg.
287: 		// Use toolCtx so cleanup() can cancel all in-flight goroutines.
288: 		s.toolWg.Add(1)
289: 		go s.executeTool(s.toolCtx, ev.ToolCallID, ev.ToolName, partID, inputMap)
290: 
291: 	case llm.EventToolResult:
292: 		// Tool results are normally handled asynchronously via executeTool goroutines.
293: 		// Some OpenAI-compatible proxies emit tool_result events directly in the stream;
294: 		// log a warning so unexpected providers are visible rather than silently ignored.
295: 		log.Printf("[session] unexpected EventToolResult for tool %q (id=%s) — provider may be emitting tool results directly in stream",
296: 			ev.ToolName, ev.ToolCallID)
297: 
298: 	case llm.EventToolError:
299: 		s.toolMu.Lock()
300: 		partID, ok := s.activeToolParts[ev.ToolCallID]
301: 		s.toolMu.Unlock()
302: 		if !ok {
303: 			break
304: 		}
305: 		_ = s.updateToolStatus(ctx, partID, store.ToolStatusError, nil, ev.Text)
306: 
307: 	case llm.EventStepFinish:
308: 		s.totalUsage = s.totalUsage.Add(ev.Usage)
309: 
310: 		// Persist step-finish part
311: 		_, _ = s.createPart(ctx, store.PartTypeStepFinish, &store.StepFinishData{
312: 			FinishReason: string(ev.FinishReason),
313: 			Usage: store.TokenSummary{
314: 				Input:      ev.Usage.Input,
315: 				Output:     ev.Usage.Output,
316: 				CacheRead:  ev.Usage.CacheRead,
317: 				CacheWrite: ev.Usage.CacheWrite,
318: 			},
319: 		})
320: 
321: 		// Check context overflow after each step
322: 		if llm.IsOverflow(ev.Usage, s.model, s.cfg) {
323: 			s.needsCompaction = true
324: 			return ProcessCompact, nil
325: 		}
326: 
327: 	case llm.EventRequestFinish:
328: 		// Final event — update assistant message with total usage
329: 		_ = s.finaliseAssistantMessage(ctx)
330: 	}
331: 
332: 	return ProcessContinue, nil
333: }

335: // executeTool runs a tool and updates the part with the result.
336: func (s *processorState) executeTool(ctx context.Context, callID, toolName, partID string, input map[string]any) {
337: 	defer s.toolWg.Done()
338: 
339: 	t, ok := s.toolMap[toolName]
340: 	if !ok {
341: 		_ = s.updateToolStatus(ctx, partID, store.ToolStatusError, nil, fmt.Sprintf("tool %q not found", toolName))
342: 		return
343: 	}
344: 
345: 	result, err := t.Execute(ctx, input)
346: 	// Guard: if cleanup already marked this part as interrupted (Status=error, Interrupted=true),
347: 	// do not overwrite — cleanup's mark takes precedence because the tool goroutine
348: 	// outlived the cleanup window and is no longer considered part of the session.
349: 	if isAlreadyInterrupted(s.store, partID) {
350: 		return
351: 	}
352: 	if err != nil {
353: 		if tf, ok := tool.IsToolFailure(err); ok {
354: 			_ = s.updateToolStatus(ctx, partID, store.ToolStatusError, nil, tf.Message)
355: 		} else {
356: 			_ = s.updateToolStatus(ctx, partID, store.ToolStatusError, nil, err.Error())
357: 		}
358: 		return
359: 	}
360: 
361: 	_ = s.updateToolCompleted(ctx, partID, toolName, callID, input, result)
362: }

364: // isAlreadyInterrupted returns true if the part has already been marked as
365: // interrupted by cleanup (Status=error AND Interrupted=true). Used to prevent
366: // executeTool from overwriting cleanup's authoritative interrupted state.
367: func isAlreadyInterrupted(s store.Store, partID string) bool {
368: 	p, err := s.GetPart(context.Background(), partID)
369: 	if err != nil {
370: 		return false
371: 	}
372: 	d, ok := store.DataAs[*store.ToolPartData](p)
373: 	if !ok {
374: 		return false
375: 	}
376: 	return d.Status == store.ToolStatusError && d.Interrupted
377: }

379: // checkDoomLoop returns true if the same tool with same args has been called
380: // DoomLoopThreshold times consecutively. Uses the shared cross-step slice.
381: func (s *processorState) checkDoomLoop(toolName, inputKey string) bool {
382: 	s.sharedRecentCallsMu.Lock()
383: 	defer s.sharedRecentCallsMu.Unlock()
384: 
385: 	*s.sharedRecentCalls = append(*s.sharedRecentCalls, recentCall{toolName: toolName, inputKey: inputKey})
386: 	if len(*s.sharedRecentCalls) > DoomLoopThreshold {
387: 		*s.sharedRecentCalls = (*s.sharedRecentCalls)[len(*s.sharedRecentCalls)-DoomLoopThreshold:]
388: 	}
389: 	if len(*s.sharedRecentCalls) < DoomLoopThreshold {
390: 		return false
391: 	}
392: 	first := (*s.sharedRecentCalls)[0]
393: 	for _, c := range (*s.sharedRecentCalls)[1:] {
394: 		if c.toolName != first.toolName || c.inputKey != first.inputKey {
395: 			return false
396: 		}
397: 	}
398: 	return true
399: }

401: // cleanup finalises any open parts when the stream ends (normally or abnormally).
402: // Aligned with processor.ts cleanup().
403: //
404: // IMPORTANT: cleanup always uses context.Background() for store writes, never
405: // the caller's ctx. When triggered by cancellation the caller's ctx is already
406: // done; using it for store operations would cause every write to fail silently
407: // in a real database backend, leaving tool parts permanently in pending state.
408: func (s *processorState) cleanup() {
409: 	ctx := context.Background()
410: 
411: 	// Finalise open text part
412: 	if s.currentTextPartID != "" {
413: 		_ = s.updateTextPart(ctx, s.currentTextPartID, s.currentTextBuf, s.currentTextStart, nowMS())
414: 		s.currentTextPartID = ""
415: 	}
416: 
417: 	// Finalise open reasoning part
418: 	if s.currentReasoningPartID != "" {
419: 		_ = s.updateReasoningPart(ctx, s.currentReasoningPartID, s.currentReasoningBuf, s.currentReasoningSignature, s.currentReasoningStart, nowMS())
420: 		s.currentReasoningPartID = ""
421: 	}
422: 
423: 	// Cancel all in-flight tool goroutines, then wait up to 250ms for them to exit.
424: 	// A single shared deadline avoids the N×250ms problem: total wait is at most
425: 	// 250ms regardless of how many tools are running.
426: 	if s.toolCancel != nil {
427: 		s.toolCancel()
428: 	}
429: 
430: 	waitDone := make(chan struct{})
431: 	go func() {
432: 		s.toolWg.Wait()
433: 		close(waitDone)
434: 	}()
435: 	select {
436: 	case <-waitDone:
437: 		// all goroutines finished cleanly
438: 	case <-time.After(250 * time.Millisecond):
439: 		// timed out — goroutines are cancelled but may not have exited yet
440: 	}
441: 
442: 	// Mark any parts that are still pending/running as interrupted.
443: 	s.toolMu.Lock()
444: 	activeSnapshot := make(map[string]string, len(s.activeToolParts))
445: 	for k, v := range s.activeToolParts {
446: 		activeSnapshot[k] = v
447: 	}
448: 	s.toolMu.Unlock()
449: 
450: 	for _, partID := range activeSnapshot {
451: 		p, err := s.store.GetPart(ctx, partID)
452: 		if err != nil {
453: 			continue
454: 		}
455: 		data, ok := store.DataAs[*store.ToolPartData](p)
456: 		if !ok || data.Status == store.ToolStatusCompleted || data.Status == store.ToolStatusError {
457: 			continue
458: 		}
459: 		_ = s.updateToolStatus(ctx, partID, store.ToolStatusError, map[string]any{"interrupted": true}, "Tool execution aborted")
460: 	}
461: }

541: 	if err != nil {

551: 		data.Error = errMsg
552: 	}
553: 	if metadata != nil {
554: 		data.Metadata = metadata
555: 		if v, ok := metadata["interrupted"].(bool); ok {
556: 			data.Interrupted = v
557: 		}
558: 	}
559: 	p.Data = data
560: 	return s.store.UpdatePart(ctx, p)
561: }

563: func (s *processorState) finaliseAssistantMessage(ctx context.Context) error {
564: 	m, err := s.store.GetMessage(ctx, s.assistantMsgID)
565: 	if err != nil {
566: 		return err
567: 	}
568: 	m.Tokens = store.TokenSummary{
569: 		Input:      s.totalUsage.Input,
570: 		Output:     s.totalUsage.Output,
571: 		CacheRead:  s.totalUsage.CacheRead,
572: 		CacheWrite: s.totalUsage.CacheWrite,
573: 	}
574: 	return s.store.UpdateMessage(ctx, m)
575: }

580: 	return time.Now().UnixMilli()
581: }

583: func marshalInput(v any) string {
584: 	b, _ := json.Marshal(v)
585: 	return string(b)
586: }
587: 
588: func toInputMap(v any) map[string]any {
589: 	if v == nil {
590: 		return nil
591: 	}
592: 	if m, ok := v.(map[string]any); ok {
593: 		return m
594: 	}
595: 	// round-trip through JSON
596: 	b, _ := json.Marshal(v)
597: 	var m map[string]any
598: 	_ = json.Unmarshal(b, &m)
599: 	return m
600: }

604: 	b := make([]byte, 16)
605: 	_, _ = rand.Read(b)

78: // RunHandle is returned by RunLoopAsync. It allows the caller to cancel the

90: // happens-before any receive on Done. No additional synchronisation is needed.

93: 	// (including Prune). Safe to start a new RunLoop on the same session after

402: 				h.closeStoreDone()

411: // buildSystem constructs the system prompt array for a request.
412: // Aligned with session/llm.ts system prompt assembly (lines 103-128):
413: //
414: //	system = [
415: //	  agentPrompt || providerPrompt,  // base — exactly one of these
416: //	  ...input.system,                // ExtraSystem
417: //	].filter(Boolean).join("\n")
418: //
419: // Priority:
420: //  1. AgentPrompt — if set, used as the sole base; provider prompt is skipped
421: //  2. Provider prompt — used when AgentPrompt is empty AND DisableProviderPrompt is false
422: //  3. ExtraSystem — always appended after the base
423: func buildSystem(input RunInput) []string {
424: 	var parts []string
425: 
426: 	switch {
427: 	case input.AgentPrompt != "":
428: 		// Agent has a custom prompt → use it, skip provider prompt entirely
429: 		parts = append(parts, input.AgentPrompt)
430: 	case !input.DisableProviderPrompt:
431: 		// No agent prompt → inject the embedded per-provider prompt
432: 		if base := SystemPromptForModel(input.Model); base != "" {
433: 			parts = append(parts, base)
434: 		}
435: 	// else: DisableProviderPrompt=true, AgentPrompt="" → no base prompt at all
436: 	}
437: 
438: 	// Always append caller-supplied extra instructions
439: 	parts = append(parts, input.ExtraSystem...)
440: 
441: 	// When session history recall is enabled (OnCompact is set), inject
442: 	// the knowledge_search guidance so the LLM knows it can retrieve
443: 	// compacted history on demand.
444: 	if input.OnCompact != nil {
445: 		parts = append(parts, PromptKnowledgeRecall)
446: 	}
447: 
448: 	// Filter empty strings
449: 	var out []string
450: 	for _, p := range parts {
451: 		if s := strings.TrimSpace(p); s != "" {
452: 			out = append(out, s)
453: 		}
454: 	}
455: 	return out
456: }

458: // hasToolCalls returns true if any part in the message is a tool call part
459: // (regardless of status — even pending means the LLM emitted a tool call).
460: func hasToolCalls(ps []*store.Part) bool {
461: 	for _, p := range ps {
462: 		if p.Type == store.PartTypeTool {
463: 			return true
464: 		}
465: 	}
466: 	return false
467: }

469: // loadMessages loads all messages and their parts for a session.
470: // Uses ListPartsBySession to fetch all parts in a single operation,
471: // avoiding N+1 queries against real database backends.
472: func loadMessages(ctx context.Context, s store.Store, sessionID string) ([]*store.Message, map[string][]*store.Part, error) {
473: 	msgs, err := s.ListMessages(ctx, sessionID)
474: 	if err != nil {
475: 		return nil, nil, err
476: 	}
477: 	allParts, err := s.ListPartsBySession(ctx, sessionID)
478: 	if err != nil {
479: 		return nil, nil, err
480: 	}
481: 	return msgs, allParts, nil
482: }

484: // markAssistantCancelled sets the Status on an assistant message after an
485: // incomplete Process() call due to ctx cancellation. It always uses
486: // context.Background() because the caller's ctx is already cancelled.
487: //
488: // Status logic:
489: //   - Has tool calls or real text content → MessageStatusInterrupted
490: //     (partial content exists; ToModelMessages preserves completed tools)
491: //   - No content at all → MessageStatusCancelled
492: //     (invisible to LLM; consecutive-user-message guard inserts a placeholder)
493: //
494: // Known race: cleanup() inside Process() waits up to 250ms for tool goroutines.
495: // After that timeout, goroutines may still be running and could write
496: // ToolStatusCompleted after ListParts reads here. In that case a completed
497: // tool result may be misclassified as Cancelled rather than Interrupted.
498: // This window is small and the consequence is limited to the next turn seeing
499: // a slightly degraded history. Eliminating it would require an unconditional
500: // wait for all tool goroutines, which is a larger change left for future work.
501: func markAssistantCancelled(s store.Store, assistantMsgID string) {
502: 	ctx := context.Background()
503: 	parts, _ := s.ListParts(ctx, assistantMsgID)
504: 	status := store.MessageStatusCancelled
505: 	if hasToolCalls(parts) || hasRealContent(parts) {

64: // SelectResult is the output of the compaction selection algorithm.
65: type SelectResult struct {

67: 	Head []*store.Message
68: 	// TailStartID is the ID of the first message in the tail to preserve verbatim.
69: 	TailStartID string
70: 	// RecentHead contains the messages belonging to the last 2 real user turns
71: 	// within Head (those immediately before the tail). These are the turns most
72: 	// likely to be mis-summarised. Nil when Head has ≤ 2 real turns (in which
73: 	// case there is nothing worth anchoring beyond what is already in the tail).

77: // Select splits a message list into head (to summarise) and tail (to keep verbatim).
78: // Aligned with packages/opencode/src/session/compaction.ts select().
79: //
80: // Algorithm:
81: //  1. Walk backwards through user turns
82: //  2. Keep the most recent tailTurns turns that fit within the preserve budget
83: //  3. Everything before the kept turns is the head to summarise
84: //
85: // allParts is used to identify compaction boundary user messages (those that
86: // contain a PartTypeCompaction part) so they are skipped, consistent with
87: // FilterCompacted. This replaces the brittle i+1-is-summary positional heuristic.
88: func Select(msgs []*store.Message, allParts map[string][]*store.Part, model llm.Model, cfg *config.Info) SelectResult {
89: 	budget := llm.PreserveRecentBudget(model, cfg)
90: 	tailTurns := DefaultTailTurns
91: 	if cfg != nil && cfg.Compaction != nil && cfg.Compaction.TailTurns != nil {
92: 		tailTurns = *cfg.Compaction.TailTurns
93: 	}
94: 
95: 	// Build list of real user turns, skipping compaction boundary messages.
96: 	// A boundary is a user message that contains a PartTypeCompaction part —
97: 	// the same criterion used by FilterCompacted.
98: 	var turns []Turn
99: 	for i, m := range msgs {
100: 		if m.Role != store.RoleUser {
101: 			continue
102: 		}
103: 		if hasPartType(allParts[m.ID], store.PartTypeCompaction) {
104: 			continue
105: 		}
106: 		turns = append(turns, Turn{UserMsgID: m.ID, StartIdx: i})
107: 	}
108: 	// Set end index for each turn
109: 	for i := range turns {
110: 		if i+1 < len(turns) {
111: 			turns[i].EndIdx = turns[i+1].StartIdx
112: 		} else {
113: 			turns[i].EndIdx = len(msgs)
114: 		}
115: 	}
116: 
117: 	// Aligned with opencode compaction.ts select():
118: 	// When there are not enough turns to split (≤ tailTurns), or when the budget
119: 	// calculation places the tail start at index 0, summarise ALL messages as the
120: 	// head with no tail preserved verbatim (tail_start_id = "").
121: 	// This avoids "nothing to summarise" errors after repeated compaction rounds
122: 	// where the visible history has already been trimmed to a small number of turns.
123: 	if len(turns) <= tailTurns {
124: 		// Still compute RecentHead (last ≤2 turns of the full head) so that Step 6
125: 		// of Compact() can write a PartTypeRecentContext excerpt onto the boundary
126: 		// message. This gives the LLM a verbatim anchor even when the entire history
127: 		// is summarised.
128: 		var recentHead []*store.Message
129: 		if len(turns) >= 1 {
130: 			startTurnIdx := len(turns) - 2
131: 			if startTurnIdx < 0 {
132: 				startTurnIdx = 0
133: 			}
134: 			recentHead = msgs[turns[startTurnIdx].StartIdx:]
135: 		}
136: 		return SelectResult{Head: msgs, TailStartID: "", RecentHead: recentHead}
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	// Determine how many of the most recent turns fit in the tail budget.
140: 	// Walk backwards through the last tailTurns turns.
141: 	tail := turns[len(turns)-tailTurns:]
142: 	totalTokens := 0
143: 	// Start of the tail — will be moved forward if budget is tight.
144: 	tailStartTurnIdx := len(turns) - tailTurns
145: 
146: 	for i := len(tail) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
147: 		t := tail[i]
148: 		size := estimateTurnTokens(msgs[t.StartIdx:t.EndIdx])
149: 		if totalTokens+size <= budget {
150: 			totalTokens += size
151: 		} else {
152: 			// This turn doesn't fit; tail starts at the next turn.
153: 			tailStartTurnIdx = len(turns) - tailTurns + i + 1
154: 			break
155: 		}
156: 	}
157: 
158: 	// Ensure tail keeps at least 1 turn.
159: 	if tailStartTurnIdx >= len(turns) {
160: 		tailStartTurnIdx = len(turns) - 1
161: 	}
162: 
163: 	tailMsgIdx := turns[tailStartTurnIdx].StartIdx
164: 	if tailMsgIdx == 0 {
165: 		// Budget covers all turns — summarise everything with no verbatim tail.
166: 		// Aligned with opencode: keep.start == 0 → head = all messages, tail_start_id = undefined.
167: 		// Still compute RecentHead for the last ≤2 turns so Step 6 writes the RC excerpt.
168: 		var recentHead []*store.Message
169: 		if len(turns) >= 1 {
170: 			startTurnIdx := tailStartTurnIdx - 2
171: 			if startTurnIdx < 0 {
172: 				startTurnIdx = 0
173: 			}
174: 			recentHead = msgs[turns[startTurnIdx].StartIdx:]
175: 		}
176: 		return SelectResult{Head: msgs, TailStartID: "", RecentHead: recentHead}
177: 	}
178: 
179: 	// Compute RecentHead: the last 2 real turns within Head (those immediately
180: 	// before the tail). Populated whenever the head is non-empty (tailStartTurnIdx >= 1)
181: 	// so the excerpt is always written after any compaction. When head has only 1 turn
182: 	// (tailStartTurnIdx == 1), recentStartIdx clamps to turns[0].StartIdx, capturing
183: 	// the single head turn verbatim.
184: 	var recentHead []*store.Message
185: 	if tailStartTurnIdx >= 1 {
186: 		recentTurnIdx := tailStartTurnIdx - 2
187: 		if recentTurnIdx < 0 {
188: 			recentTurnIdx = 0
189: 		}
190: 		recentStartIdx := turns[recentTurnIdx].StartIdx
191: 		recentHead = msgs[recentStartIdx:tailMsgIdx]
192: 	}
193: 
194: 	return SelectResult{
195: 		Head:        msgs[:tailMsgIdx],
196: 		TailStartID: msgs[tailMsgIdx].ID,
197: 		RecentHead:  recentHead,
198: 	}
199: }

201: // estimateTurnTokens estimates the token count for a slice of messages.
202: // Uses stored token counts when available, falling back to a character heuristic.
203: func estimateTurnTokens(msgs []*store.Message) int {
204: 	total := 0
205: 	for _, m := range msgs {
206: 		t := m.Tokens
207: 		if n := t.Input + t.Output + t.CacheRead + t.CacheWrite; n > 0 {
208: 			total += n
209: 		} else {
210: 			total += 100 // fallback for messages without stored usage data
211: 		}
212: 	}
213: 	return total
214: }

222: 	}
