10: // ToModelMessages converts stored messages and their parts into the canonical
11: // llm.Message slice to be sent to the provider.
12: // Aligned with packages/opencode/src/session/message-v2.ts toModelMessagesEffect().
13: //
14: // Key rules:
15: //   - User messages: text parts → text content; compaction parts → "What did we do so far?"
16: //   - recent-context parts → verbatim excerpt (stripped when StripMedia=true)
17: //   - Assistant messages: skip if errored (unless AbortedError with content)
18: //   - Tool parts: completed → output-available; error/interrupted → output-error
19: //   - Compacted tool output → "[Old tool result content cleared]"
20: //   - Pending/running tool parts (interrupted) → "[Tool execution was interrupted]"
21: //
22: // Interrupted assistant messages (Status=interrupted/cancelled):
23: //   - cancelled (no content): completely invisible to LLM; a silent " " placeholder
24: //     is injected between any two consecutive user messages to satisfy protocol.
25: //   - interrupted + no tool calls: keep partial text as-is; LLM infers naturally.
26: //   - interrupted + has tool calls: keep completed tools, discard pending ones,
27: //     append "[Assistant turn was interrupted by user]" so LLM does not retry.
28: func ToModelMessages(msgs []*store.Message, parts map[string][]*store.Part) ([]llm.Message, error) {
29: 	// Pre-filter: remove user+assistant pairs where the assistant never produced
30: 	// content (cancelled before response, or LLM transport error with no content).
31: 	// These pairs are completely invisible to the LLM. Removing them here prevents
32: 	// the alternating-role guard below from inserting a " " placeholder, which
33: 	// proxies reject as invalid assistant content.
34: 	filtered := make([]*store.Message, 0, len(msgs))
35: 	for i := 0; i < len(msgs); i++ {
36: 		m := msgs[i]
37: 		if m.Role == store.RoleAssistant {
38: 			ps := parts[m.ID]
39: 			drop := false
40: 			if m.Status == store.MessageStatusCancelled {
41: 				drop = true
42: 			} else if m.Error != nil && !hasRealContent(ps) {
43: 				drop = true
44: 			}
45: 			if drop {
46: 				// Also drop the preceding user message if it is there.
47: 				if len(filtered) > 0 && filtered[len(filtered)-1].Role == store.RoleUser {
48: 					filtered = filtered[:len(filtered)-1]
49: 				}
50: 				continue
51: 			}
52: 		}
53: 		filtered = append(filtered, m)
54: 	}
55: 
56: 	var out []llm.Message
57: 
58: 	for _, m := range filtered {
59: 		ps := parts[m.ID]
60: 
61: 		switch m.Role {
62: 		case store.RoleUser:
63: 			userParts := buildUserParts(ps, ToModelOptions{})
64: 			if len(userParts) == 0 {
65: 				continue
66: 			}
67: 			// Protocol fix: two consecutive user messages are invalid on both
68: 			// Anthropic and OpenAI. This can still happen if an interrupted
69: 			// assistant message had no usable content (buildAssistantPartsInterrupted
70: 			// returns empty). Insert a single-space placeholder — but only as a last
71: 			// resort; the pre-filter above eliminates the common cancelled/error cases.
72: 			if len(out) > 0 && out[len(out)-1].Role == llm.RoleUser {
73: 				out = append(out, llm.Message{
74: 					Role:    llm.RoleAssistant,
75: 					Content: []llm.ContentPart{llm.NewTextPart(" ")},
76: 				})
77: 			}
78: 			out = append(out, llm.Message{
79: 				ID:      m.ID,
80: 				Role:    llm.RoleUser,
81: 				Content: userParts,
82: 			})
83: 
84: 		case store.RoleAssistant:
85: 			// Interrupted: partial content exists. Handle tool-call case specially.
86: 			if m.Status == store.MessageStatusInterrupted {
87: 				assistantParts, toolResultMsgs := buildAssistantPartsInterrupted(ps)
88: 				if len(assistantParts) == 0 {
89: 					continue
90: 				}
91: 				out = append(out, llm.Message{
92: 					ID:      m.ID,
93: 					Role:    llm.RoleAssistant,
94: 					Content: assistantParts,
95: 				})
96: 				if len(toolResultMsgs) > 0 {
97: 					out = append(out, llm.Message{
98: 						Role:    llm.RoleTool,
99: 						Content: toolResultMsgs,
100: 					})
101: 				}
102: 				continue
103: 			}
104: 
105: 			// Normal path: skip errored/empty assistant messages.
106: 			if m.Error != nil {
107: 				if !hasRealContent(ps) {
108: 					continue
109: 				}
110: 			}
111: 
112: 			assistantParts, toolResultMsgs := buildAssistantParts(m, ps)
113: 			if len(assistantParts) == 0 {
114: 				continue
115: 			}
116: 			out = append(out, llm.Message{
117: 				ID:      m.ID,
118: 				Role:    llm.RoleAssistant,
119: 				Content: assistantParts,
120: 			})
121: 
122: 			// Inject tool results as a synthetic tool-role message
123: 			// (required by Anthropic; OpenAI expects them interleaved with assistant messages)
124: 			if len(toolResultMsgs) > 0 {
125: 				out = append(out, llm.Message{
126: 					Role:    llm.RoleTool,
127: 					Content: toolResultMsgs,
128: 				})
129: 			}
130: 		}
131: 	}
132: 
133: 	return out, nil
134: }
135: 
136: // buildAssistantPartsInterrupted handles an assistant message whose turn was
137: // cut short by Cancel() after some content had been emitted.
138: //
139: // Rules (per design):
140: //   - Text/reasoning parts: always kept as-is (LLM infers naturally from partial text).
141: //   - Tool parts with Status=completed: kept with their output.
142: //   - Tool parts with Status=pending/running/error(interrupted): discarded from
143: //     the assistant side AND from the tool-result side (no dangling tool calls).
144: //   - If any tool call was present (completed or not), a single
145: //     "[Assistant turn was interrupted by user]" notice is inserted BEFORE the
146: //     tool call parts so the LLM does not attempt to retry incomplete tool calls.
147: //     Text before tool use is the safe ordering for Anthropic.
148: func buildAssistantPartsInterrupted(ps []*store.Part) ([]llm.ContentPart, []llm.ContentPart) {
149: 	// Collect text/reasoning and tool parts separately so we can order them:
150: 	// [text/reasoning] → [interruption notice] → [tool calls]
151: 	var textParts []llm.ContentPart
152: 	var toolCallParts []llm.ContentPart
153: 	var toolResults []llm.ContentPart
154: 	hadAnyTool := false
155: 
156: 	for _, p := range ps {
157: 		switch p.Type {
158: 		case store.PartTypeText:
159: 			d, ok := store.DataAs[*store.TextPartData](p)
160: 			if !ok {
161: 				continue
162: 			}
163: 			text := d.Text
164: 			if text == "" {
165: 				text = " "
166: 			}
167: 			textParts = append(textParts, llm.NewTextPart(text))
168: 
169: 		case store.PartTypeReasoning:
170: 			d, ok := store.DataAs[*store.ReasoningPartData](p)
171: 			if !ok {
172: 				continue
173: 			}
174: 			if d.Text != "" {
175: 				textParts = append(textParts, llm.NewReasoningPart(d.Text, d.Signature))
176: 			}
177: 
178: 		case store.PartTypeTool:
179: 			hadAnyTool = true
180: 			d, ok := store.DataAs[*store.ToolPartData](p)
181: 			if !ok {
182: 				continue
183: 			}
184: 			// Only include tool calls that completed — drop pending/running/interrupted.
185: 			if d.Status != store.ToolStatusCompleted {
186: 				continue
187: 			}
188: 			inputMap := d.Input
189: 			if inputMap == nil {
190: 				inputMap = map[string]any{}
191: 			}
192: 			toolCallParts = append(toolCallParts, llm.NewToolCallPart(d.CallID, d.Tool, inputMap))
193: 			toolResults = append(toolResults, llm.NewToolResultPart(d.CallID, d.Tool, buildToolResult(d)))
194: 		}
195: 	}
196: 
197: 	// Assemble: text/reasoning first, then interruption notice (if tools were
198: 	// involved), then tool call parts. Text before tool use is the safe
199: 	// content ordering for Anthropic's validation rules.
200: 	//
201: 	// Special case: the LLM emitted tool calls (hadAnyTool=true) but none
202: 	// completed before cancellation (toolCallParts is empty). We cannot keep
203: 	// the text parts alone because the assistant message would then reference
204: 	// tool calls that have no corresponding tool-result, creating a broken
205: 	// history fragment. Drop the entire turn; the consecutive-user-message
206: 	// guard in ToModelMessages inserts a " " placeholder so the protocol
207: 	// alternating-role requirement is still satisfied.
208: 	//
209: 	// Note: this is distinct from the "interrupted + no tool calls" case
210: 	// (hadAnyTool=false), where partial text is kept as-is because the LLM
211: 	// never issued a tool call and there is no tool-result gap to worry about.
212: 	if hadAnyTool && len(toolCallParts) == 0 {
213: 		return nil, nil
214: 	}
215: 
216: 	assistantParts := textParts
217: 	if hadAnyTool {
218: 		assistantParts = append(assistantParts, llm.NewTextPart("[Assistant turn was interrupted by user]"))
219: 		assistantParts = append(assistantParts, toolCallParts...)
220: 	}
221: 
222: 	return assistantParts, toolResults
223: }
224: 
225: // buildUserParts converts user message parts into LLM content parts.
226: // opts.StripMedia=true suppresses PartTypeRecentContext (used during summary
227: // generation to avoid feeding previous excerpts to the summary LLM).
228: func buildUserParts(ps []*store.Part, opts ToModelOptions) []llm.ContentPart {
229: 	var parts []llm.ContentPart
230: 	for _, p := range ps {
231: 		switch p.Type {
232: 		case store.PartTypeText:
233: 			d, ok := store.DataAs[*store.TextPartData](p)
234: 			if !ok {
235: 				continue
236: 			}
237: 			if d.Text != "" {
238: 				parts = append(parts, llm.NewTextPart(d.Text))
239: 			}
240: 		case store.PartTypeCompaction:
241: 			// Compaction boundary — represents summarised history
242: 			parts = append(parts, llm.NewTextPart("What did we do so far?"))
243: 		case store.PartTypeRecentContext:
244: 			if opts.StripMedia {
245: 				continue // omit excerpt when building input for the summary LLM
246: 			}
247: 			d, ok := store.DataAs[*store.RecentContextPartData](p)
248: 			if ok && d.Excerpt != "" {
249: 				parts = append(parts, llm.NewTextPart(d.Excerpt))
250: 			}
251: 		case store.PartTypeAgent:
252: 			parts = append(parts, llm.NewTextPart("The following tool was executed by the user"))
253: 		}
254: 	}
255: 	return parts
256: }
257: 
258: // buildAssistantParts converts assistant message parts into LLM content parts.
259: // Returns (assistantParts, toolResultParts).
260: // Tool results are returned separately so they can be injected as a tool-role message.
261: func buildAssistantParts(m *store.Message, ps []*store.Part) ([]llm.ContentPart, []llm.ContentPart) {
262: 	var assistantParts []llm.ContentPart
263: 	var toolResults []llm.ContentPart
264: 
265: 	for _, p := range ps {
266: 		switch p.Type {
267: 		case store.PartTypeText:
268: 			d, ok := store.DataAs[*store.TextPartData](p)
269: 			if !ok {
270: 				continue
271: 			}
272: 			text := d.Text
273: 			if text == "" {
274: 				text = " " // preserve empty text to avoid Anthropic validation errors
275: 			}
276: 			assistantParts = append(assistantParts, llm.NewTextPart(text))
277: 
278: 		case store.PartTypeReasoning:
279: 			d, ok := store.DataAs[*store.ReasoningPartData](p)
280: 			if !ok {
281: 				continue
282: 			}
283: 			if d.Text != "" {
284: 				assistantParts = append(assistantParts, llm.NewReasoningPart(d.Text, d.Signature))
285: 			}
286: 
287: 		case store.PartTypeTool:
288: 			d, ok := store.DataAs[*store.ToolPartData](p)
289: 			if !ok {
290: 				continue
291: 			}
292: 
293: 			inputMap := d.Input
294: 			if inputMap == nil {
295: 				inputMap = map[string]any{}
296: 			}
297: 
298: 			// Tool call on the assistant side
299: 			assistantParts = append(assistantParts, llm.NewToolCallPart(d.CallID, d.Tool, inputMap))
300: 
301: 			// Tool result on the tool side (will be injected separately)
302: 			result := buildToolResult(d)
303: 			toolResults = append(toolResults, llm.NewToolResultPart(d.CallID, d.Tool, result))
304: 
305: 		case store.PartTypeStepStart:
306: 			// step-start parts are structural; not sent to LLM
307: 		}
308: 	}
309: 
310: 	return assistantParts, toolResults
311: }
312: 
313: // buildToolResult converts a ToolPartData into a ToolResult for the LLM context.
314: // Aligned with message-v2.ts tool part conversion logic.
315: func buildToolResult(d *store.ToolPartData) *llm.ToolResult {
316: 	switch d.Status {
317: 	case store.ToolStatusCompleted:
318: 		output := d.Output
319: 		if d.Compacted > 0 {
320: 			// Output was pruned to save context space
321: 			output = "[Old tool result content cleared]"
322: 		}
323: 		return llm.NewTextResult(output)
324: 
325: 	case store.ToolStatusError:
326: 		// If interrupted but has partial output, use output-available
327: 		if d.Interrupted && d.Output != "" {
328: 			return llm.NewTextResult(d.Output)
329: 		}
330: 		errMsg := d.Error
331: 		if errMsg == "" {
332: 			errMsg = "Tool execution failed"
333: 		}
334: 		return llm.NewErrorResult(errMsg)
335: 
336: 	case store.ToolStatusPending, store.ToolStatusRunning:
337: 		// Tool was interrupted before completing
338: 		return llm.NewErrorResult("[Tool execution was interrupted]")
339: 	}
340: 
341: 	return llm.NewErrorResult(fmt.Sprintf("unknown tool status: %s", d.Status))
342: }
343: 
344: // hasRealContent returns true if the message has non-tool, non-empty parts.
345: // Used to decide whether to keep an errored assistant message in context.
346: func hasRealContent(ps []*store.Part) bool {
347: 	for _, p := range ps {
348: 		if p.Type == store.PartTypeText {
349: 			if d, ok := store.DataAs[*store.TextPartData](p); ok && d.Text != "" {
350: 				return true
351: 			}
352: 		}
353: 		if p.Type == store.PartTypeReasoning {
354: 			if d, ok := store.DataAs[*store.ReasoningPartData](p); ok && d.Text != "" {
355: 				return true
356: 			}
357: 		}
358: 	}
359: 	return false
360: }
361: 
362: // FilterCompacted returns only the messages that are visible after compaction.
363: // Aligned with message-v2.ts filterCompacted().
364: //
365: // Rule: find the most recent *complete* compaction pair (boundary user message
366: // + summary assistant message). Walking backward avoids mis-pairing a boundary
367: // from one round with a summary from another on partial failures.
368: func FilterCompacted(msgs []*store.Message, parts map[string][]*store.Part) []*store.Message {
369: 	for i := len(msgs) - 1; i >= 1; i-- {
370: 		if msgs[i].Role != store.RoleAssistant || !msgs[i].Summary {
371: 			continue
372: 		}
373: 		// Found a summary — look for its boundary user message just before it.
374: 		for j := i - 1; j >= 0; j-- {
375: 			if msgs[j].Role != store.RoleUser {
376: 				continue
377: 			}
378: 			ps := parts[msgs[j].ID]
379: 			for _, p := range ps {
380: 				if p.Type == store.PartTypeCompaction {
381: 					out := make([]*store.Message, 0, len(msgs)-j)
382: 					out = append(out, msgs[j])    // compaction boundary user msg
383: 					out = append(out, msgs[i:]...) // summary + tail
384: 					return out
385: 				}
386: 			}
387: 			// A real user message between summary and boundary — no match, stop.
388: 			break
389: 		}
390: 	}
391: 	return msgs
392: }

396: 	roleUser      = "user"
397: 	roleAssistant = "assistant"
398: )

184: // RecentContextPartData holds a verbatim excerpt of the turns immediately
185: // preceding the tail at the time of compaction. Attached to the compaction
186: // boundary message so the LLM has a fine-grained anchor without needing to
187: // call knowledge_search.
188: type RecentContextPartData struct {
189: 	Excerpt string // verbatim rendered excerpt of the last 2 turns of head
190: }
191: 
192: // RetryPartData records a retry attempt.
193: type RetryPartData struct {
194: 	Attempt int
195: 	Message string
196: }
197: 
198: // DataAs extracts the typed payload from a Part.
199: // It centralises the runtime type assertion so callers get a single point
200: // of failure rather than silent ok=false branches scattered across the
201: // session package.
202: //
203: // Two-phase lookup:
204: //  1. Direct type assertion — works for the memory store which holds typed Go pointers.
205: //  2. JSON round-trip fallback — handles stores (SQLite, Redis, etc.) that
206: //     deserialise Part.Data as map[string]any. Without this fallback, every
207: //     DataAs call on a SQL-backed store would silently return ok=false,
208: //     dropping all tool/text/reasoning data.
209: //
210: // Usage:
211: //
212: //	d, ok := store.DataAs[*store.ToolPartData](p)
213: func DataAs[T any](p *Part) (T, bool) {
214: 	if p.Data == nil {
215: 		var zero T
216: 		return zero, false
217: 	}
218: 	if v, ok := p.Data.(T); ok {
219: 		return v, ok
220: 	}
221: 	// JSON round-trip fallback for stores that deserialise Data as map[string]any.
222: 	b, err := json.Marshal(p.Data)
223: 	if err != nil {
224: 		var zero T
225: 		return zero, false
226: 	}
227: 	var v T
228: 	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &v); err != nil {
229: 		var zero T
230: 		return zero, false
231: 	}
232: 	return v, true
233: }

34: func New(apiKey, baseURL string, extraHeaders map[string]string) *Provider {

47: // NewFromConfig builds a Provider from config + auth store.
48: func NewFromConfig(cfg *config.ProviderInfo, authStore *auth.Store) (*Provider, error) {
49: 	apiKey, _ := auth.ResolveKey(ProviderID, EnvVars, authStore)
50: 	baseURL := ""
51: 
52: 	if cfg != nil {
53: 		if cfg.Options != nil {
54: 			if cfg.Options.APIKey != "" {
55: 				apiKey = cfg.Options.APIKey
56: 			}
57: 			if cfg.Options.BaseURL != "" {
58: 				baseURL = cfg.Options.BaseURL
59: 			}
60: 		}
61: 		if cfg.API != "" {
62: 			baseURL = cfg.API
63: 		}
64: 	}
65: 
66: 	if apiKey == "" {
67: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("anthropic: no API key found (set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or configure in opencode.json)")
68: 	}
69: 
70: 	extraHeaders := map[string]string{
71: 		"anthropic-beta": "interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14",
72: 	}
73: 	return New(apiKey, baseURL, extraHeaders), nil
74: }

76: func (p *Provider) ID() string { return ProviderID }

78: // Factory is a provider.Factory-compatible function for this package.
79: // Register it with a provider.Registry via registry.RegisterFactory(ProviderID, anthropic.Factory).
80: var Factory = func(cfg *config.ProviderInfo, authStore *auth.Store) (llm.Provider, error) {

84: // Stream implements llm.Provider.
85: func (p *Provider) Stream(ctx context.Context, req llm.Request) (<-chan llm.Event, error) {
86: 	params, err := buildParams(req)
87: 	if err != nil {
88: 		return nil, err
89: 	}
90: 
91: 	stream := p.client.Messages.NewStreaming(ctx, params)
92: 	ch := make(chan llm.Event, 32)
93: 	go func() {
94: 		defer close(ch)
95: 		runStream(ctx, stream, ch)
96: 	}()
97: 	return ch, nil
98: }

100: // buildParams converts a canonical llm.Request into anthropic.MessageNewParams.
101: func buildParams(req llm.Request) (anthropic.MessageNewParams, error) {
102: 	params := anthropic.MessageNewParams{
103: 		Model:     anthropic.Model(req.Model.APIID),
104: 		MaxTokens: int64(effectiveMaxTokens(req)),
105: 	}
106: 
107: 	// System prompt — keep as separate blocks to preserve per-entry cache granularity.
108: 	if len(req.System) > 0 {
109: 		sysBlocks := make([]anthropic.TextBlockParam, 0, len(req.System))
110: 		for _, s := range req.System {
111: 			if s != "" {
112: 				sysBlocks = append(sysBlocks, anthropic.TextBlockParam{Text: s})
113: 			}
114: 		}
115: 		params.System = sysBlocks
116: 	}
117: 
118: 	// Temperature
119: 	if req.Options.Temperature != nil {
120: 		params.Temperature = anthropic.Float(*req.Options.Temperature)
121: 	}
122: 
123: 	// Tool choice
124: 	switch req.ToolChoice {
125: 	case llm.ToolChoiceNone:
126: 		params.ToolChoice = anthropic.ToolChoiceUnionParam{
127: 			OfNone: &anthropic.ToolChoiceNoneParam{Type: "none"},
128: 		}
129: 	case llm.ToolChoiceRequired:
130: 		params.ToolChoice = anthropic.ToolChoiceUnionParam{
131: 			OfAny: &anthropic.ToolChoiceAnyParam{Type: "any"},
132: 		}
133: 	}
134: 
135: 	// Tools
136: 	if len(req.Tools) > 0 {
137: 		tools := make([]anthropic.ToolUnionParam, 0, len(req.Tools))
138: 		for _, t := range req.Tools {
139: 			schemaBytes, err := json.Marshal(t.InputSchema)
140: 			if err != nil {
141: 				return params, fmt.Errorf("tool %q: marshal schema: %w", t.Name, err)
142: 			}
143: 			var schemaParam anthropic.ToolInputSchemaParam
144: 			if err := json.Unmarshal(schemaBytes, &schemaParam); err != nil {
145: 				return params, fmt.Errorf("tool %q: unmarshal schema param: %w", t.Name, err)
146: 			}
147: 			tools = append(tools, anthropic.ToolUnionParam{
148: 				OfTool: &anthropic.ToolParam{
149: 					Name:        t.Name,
150: 					Description: anthropic.String(t.Description),
151: 					InputSchema: schemaParam,
152: 				},
153: 			})
154: 		}
155: 		params.Tools = tools
156: 	}
157: 
158: 	// Messages
159: 	msgs, err := convertMessages(req.Messages)
160: 	if err != nil {
161: 		return params, err
162: 	}
163: 	params.Messages = msgs
164: 
165: 	return params, nil
166: }
167: 
168: func effectiveMaxTokens(req llm.Request) int {
169: 	if req.Options.MaxTokens > 0 {
170: 		return req.Options.MaxTokens
171: 	}
172: 	return llm.MaxOutputTokens(req.Model)
173: }
174: 
175: // convertMessages converts canonical messages to Anthropic's format.
176: func convertMessages(msgs []llm.Message) ([]anthropic.MessageParam, error) {
177: 	var out []anthropic.MessageParam
178: 	for _, m := range msgs {
179: 		switch m.Role {
180: 		case llm.RoleUser:
181: 			blocks, err := userBlocks(m.Content)
182: 			if err != nil {
183: 				return nil, err
184: 			}
185: 			out = append(out, anthropic.NewUserMessage(blocks...))
186: 		case llm.RoleAssistant:
187: 			blocks, err := assistantBlocks(m.Content)
188: 			if err != nil {
189: 				return nil, err
190: 			}
191: 			out = append(out, anthropic.NewAssistantMessage(blocks...))
192: 		case llm.RoleTool:
193: 			// Tool results are injected as a user message in Anthropic's protocol
194: 			blocks, err := toolResultBlocks(m.Content)
195: 			if err != nil {
196: 				return nil, err
197: 			}
198: 			if len(blocks) > 0 {
199: 				out = append(out, anthropic.NewUserMessage(blocks...))
200: 			}
201: 		}
202: 	}
203: 	return out, nil
204: }
205: 
206: func userBlocks(parts []llm.ContentPart) ([]anthropic.ContentBlockParamUnion, error) {
207: 	var blocks []anthropic.ContentBlockParamUnion
208: 	for _, p := range parts {
209: 		switch p.Type {
210: 		case llm.PartTypeText:
211: 			if p.Text != "" {
212: 				blocks = append(blocks, anthropic.NewTextBlock(p.Text))
213: 			}
214: 		case llm.PartTypeImage:
215: 			if len(p.Data) > 0 {
216: 				encoded := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(p.Data)
217: 				blocks = append(blocks, anthropic.NewImageBlockBase64(p.MediaType, encoded))
218: 			} else if p.URL != "" {
219: 				blocks = append(blocks, anthropic.NewImageBlock(anthropic.URLImageSourceParam{URL: p.URL}))
220: 			}
221: 		}
222: 	}
223: 	return blocks, nil
224: }
225: 
226: func toolResultBlocks(parts []llm.ContentPart) ([]anthropic.ContentBlockParamUnion, error) {
227: 	var blocks []anthropic.ContentBlockParamUnion
228: 	for _, p := range parts {
229: 		if p.Type != llm.PartTypeToolResult {
230: 			continue
231: 		}
232: 		resultText := ""
233: 		isError := false
234: 		if p.Result != nil {
235: 			isError = p.Result.Type == llm.ToolResultTypeError
236: 			switch v := p.Result.Value.(type) {
237: 			case string:
238: 				resultText = v
239: 			default:
240: 				b, _ := json.Marshal(p.Result.Value)
241: 				resultText = string(b)
242: 			}
243: 		}
244: 		blocks = append(blocks, anthropic.NewToolResultBlock(p.ToolCallID, resultText, isError))
245: 	}
246: 	return blocks, nil
247: }
248: 
249: func assistantBlocks(parts []llm.ContentPart) ([]anthropic.ContentBlockParamUnion, error) {
250: 	var blocks []anthropic.ContentBlockParamUnion
251: 	for _, p := range parts {
252: 		switch p.Type {
253: 		case llm.PartTypeText:
254: 			if p.Text != "" {
255: 				blocks = append(blocks, anthropic.NewTextBlock(p.Text))
256: 			}
257: 		case llm.PartTypeToolCall:
258: 			blocks = append(blocks, anthropic.NewToolUseBlock(p.ToolCallID, p.Input, p.ToolName))
259: 		case llm.PartTypeReasoning:
260: 			if p.Text != "" {
261: 				blocks = append(blocks, anthropic.ContentBlockParamUnion{
262: 					OfThinking: &anthropic.ThinkingBlockParam{
263: 						Type:      "thinking",
264: 						Thinking:  p.Text,
265: 						Signature: p.Signature,
266: 					},
267: 				})
268: 			}
269: 		}
270: 	}
271: 	return blocks, nil
272: }
273: 
274: // runStream processes the Anthropic streaming response and emits canonical events.
275: func runStream(ctx context.Context, stream *ssestream.Stream[anthropic.MessageStreamEventUnion], out chan<- llm.Event) {
276: 	defer stream.Close()
277: 
278: 	out <- llm.Event{Type: llm.EventRequestStart}
279: 
280: 	var usage llm.TokenUsage
281: 	currentToolID := ""
282: 	currentToolName := ""
283: 	var toolInputBuf []byte
284: 	inText := false
285: 	inReasoning := false
286: 	reasoningSignature := ""
287: 
288: 	for stream.Next() {
289: 		raw := stream.Current()
290: 		switch ev := raw.AsAny().(type) {
291: 		case anthropic.MessageStartEvent:
292: 			out <- llm.Event{Type: llm.EventStepStart}
293: 			usage.Input = int(ev.Message.Usage.InputTokens)
294: 			usage.CacheRead = int(ev.Message.Usage.CacheReadInputTokens)
295: 			usage.CacheWrite = int(ev.Message.Usage.CacheCreationInputTokens)
296: 
297: 		case anthropic.ContentBlockStartEvent:
298: 			switch block := ev.ContentBlock.AsAny().(type) {
299: 			case anthropic.TextBlock:
300: 				_ = block
301: 				inText = true
302: 				out <- llm.Event{Type: llm.EventTextStart}
303: 			case anthropic.ToolUseBlock:
304: 				currentToolID = block.ID
305: 				currentToolName = block.Name
306: 				toolInputBuf = nil
307: 				out <- llm.Event{
308: 					Type:       llm.EventToolInputStart,
309: 					ToolCallID: currentToolID,
310: 					ToolName:   currentToolName,
311: 				}
312: 			case anthropic.ThinkingBlock:
313: 				reasoningSignature = block.Signature
314: 				inReasoning = true
315: 			}
316: 
317: 		case anthropic.ContentBlockDeltaEvent:
318: 			switch delta := ev.Delta.AsAny().(type) {
319: 			case anthropic.TextDelta:
320: 				out <- llm.Event{Type: llm.EventTextDelta, Text: delta.Text}
321: 			case anthropic.InputJSONDelta:
322: 				toolInputBuf = append(toolInputBuf, delta.PartialJSON...)
323: 				out <- llm.Event{
324: 					Type:       llm.EventToolInputDelta,
325: 					ToolCallID: currentToolID,
326: 					ToolName:   currentToolName,
327: 					Text:       delta.PartialJSON,
328: 				}
329: 			case anthropic.ThinkingDelta:
330: 				out <- llm.Event{Type: llm.EventReasoningDelta, Text: delta.Thinking}
331: 			}
332: 
333: 		case anthropic.ContentBlockStopEvent:
334: 			_ = ev
335: 			if inText {
336: 				out <- llm.Event{Type: llm.EventTextEnd}
337: 				inText = false
338: 			} else if inReasoning {
339: 				out <- llm.Event{Type: llm.EventReasoningEnd, Signature: reasoningSignature}
340: 				inReasoning = false
341: 				reasoningSignature = ""
342: 			} else if currentToolID != "" {
343: 				var input any
344: 				if len(toolInputBuf) > 0 {
345: 					_ = json.Unmarshal(toolInputBuf, &input)
346: 				}
347: 				out <- llm.Event{
348: 					Type:       llm.EventToolCall,
349: 					ToolCallID: currentToolID,
350: 					ToolName:   currentToolName,
351: 					Input:      input,
352: 				}
353: 				currentToolID = ""
354: 				currentToolName = ""
355: 				toolInputBuf = nil
356: 			}
357: 
358: 		case anthropic.MessageDeltaEvent:
359: 			usage.Output += int(ev.Usage.OutputTokens)
360: 			out <- llm.Event{
361: 				Type:         llm.EventStepFinish,
362: 				Usage:        usage,
363: 				FinishReason: mapStopReason(string(ev.Delta.StopReason)),
364: 			}
365: 
366: 		case anthropic.MessageStopEvent:
367: 			_ = ev
368: 			// stream done
369: 		}
370: 
371: 		select {
372: 		case <-ctx.Done():
373: 			out <- llm.Event{Type: llm.EventError, Err: ctx.Err()}
374: 			return
375: 		default:
376: 		}
377: 	}
378: 
379: 	if err := stream.Err(); err != nil {
380: 		out <- llm.Event{Type: llm.EventError, Err: classifyError(err)}
381: 		return
382: 	}
383: 
384: 	out <- llm.Event{
385: 		Type:         llm.EventRequestFinish,
386: 		Usage:        usage,
387: 		FinishReason: llm.FinishReasonStop,
388: 	}
389: }
390: 
391: func mapStopReason(reason string) llm.FinishReason {
392: 	switch reason {
393: 	case "end_turn":
394: 		return llm.FinishReasonStop
395: 	case "tool_use":
396: 		return llm.FinishReasonToolCalls
397: 	case "max_tokens":
398: 		return llm.FinishReasonLength
399: 	}
400: 	return llm.FinishReasonOther
401: }
402: 
403: func classifyError(err error) error {
404: 	if err == nil {
405: 		return nil
406: 	}
407: 	var apiErr *anthropic.Error
408: 	if errors.As(err, &apiErr) {
409: 		headers := http.Header{}
410: 		if apiErr.Response != nil {
411: 			headers = apiErr.Response.Header
412: 		}
413: 		return llm.ClassifyHTTPError(ProviderID, apiErr.StatusCode, apiErr.Error(), headers)
414: 	}
415: 	return &llm.LLMError{
416: 		Kind:        llm.ErrTransport,
417: 		Message:     err.Error(),
418: 		IsRetryable: false,
419: 	}
420: }

125: 		params.MaxCompletionTokens = openai.Int(int64(req.Options.MaxTokens))
126: 	} else {
127: 		params.MaxCompletionTokens = openai.Int(int64(llm.MaxOutputTokens(req.Model)))
128: 	}
129: 
130: 	if req.Options.Temperature != nil {
131: 		params.Temperature = openai.Float(*req.Options.Temperature)
132: 	}
133: 
134: 	msgs, err := convertMessages(req.System, req.Messages)
135: 	if err != nil {
136: 		return params, err
137: 	}
138: 	params.Messages = msgs
139: 
140: 	if len(req.Tools) > 0 {
141: 		tools := make([]openai.ChatCompletionToolParam, 0, len(req.Tools))
142: 		for _, t := range req.Tools {
143: 			schemaBytes, err := json.Marshal(t.InputSchema)
144: 			if err != nil {
145: 				return params, fmt.Errorf("tool %q: marshal schema: %w", t.Name, err)
146: 			}
147: 			var schemaMap map[string]any
148: 			_ = json.Unmarshal(schemaBytes, &schemaMap)
149: 			tools = append(tools, openai.ChatCompletionToolParam{
150: 				Function: openai.FunctionDefinitionParam{
151: 					Name:        t.Name,
152: 					Description: openai.String(t.Description),
153: 					Parameters:  openai.FunctionParameters(schemaMap),
154: 				},
155: 			})
156: 		}
157: 		params.Tools = tools
158: 
159: 		switch req.ToolChoice {
160: 		case llm.ToolChoiceNone:
161: 			params.ToolChoice = openai.ChatCompletionToolChoiceOptionUnionParam{
162: 				OfAuto: openai.String("none"),
163: 			}
164: 		case llm.ToolChoiceRequired:
165: 			params.ToolChoice = openai.ChatCompletionToolChoiceOptionUnionParam{
166: 				OfAuto: openai.String("required"),
167: 			}
168: 		}
169: 	}
170: 
171: 	return params, nil
172: }

174: func convertMessages(system []string, msgs []llm.Message) ([]openai.ChatCompletionMessageParamUnion, error) {
175: 	var out []openai.ChatCompletionMessageParamUnion
176: 
177: 	for _, s := range system {
178: 		if s != "" {
179: 			out = append(out, openai.SystemMessage(s))
180: 		}
181: 	}
182: 
183: 	for _, m := range msgs {
184: 		switch m.Role {
185: 		case llm.RoleUser:
186: 			// Build a multi-part content array when the message contains image or
187: 			// file parts; otherwise fall back to a plain text message.
188: 			var parts []openai.ChatCompletionContentPartUnionParam
189: 			for _, p := range m.Content {
190: 			switch p.Type {
191: 			case llm.PartTypeText:
192: 				if p.Text != "" {
193: 					parts = append(parts, openai.TextContentPart(p.Text))
194: 				}
195: 				case llm.PartTypeImage:
196: 					if p.URL != "" {
197: 						parts = append(parts, openai.ImageContentPart(
198: 							openai.ChatCompletionContentPartImageImageURLParam{URL: p.URL},
199: 						))
200: 					} else if len(p.Data) > 0 && p.MediaType != "" {
201: 						parts = append(parts, openai.ImageContentPart(
202: 							openai.ChatCompletionContentPartImageImageURLParam{
203: 								URL: "data:" + p.MediaType + ";base64," + encodeBase64(p.Data),
204: 							},
205: 						))
206: 					}
207: 				// PartTypeFile: no standard OpenAI multi-modal file part; skip silently
208: 				}
209: 			}
210: 			if len(parts) == 0 {
211: 				// No renderable content (e.g. file-only message). Skip rather
212: 				// than sending an empty string that would confuse the model.
213: 				continue
214: 			} else {
215: 				out = append(out, openai.UserMessage(parts))
216: 			}
217: 
218: 		case llm.RoleAssistant:
219: 			text := ""
220: 			var toolCalls []openai.ChatCompletionMessageToolCallParam
221: 			for _, p := range m.Content {
222: 				switch p.Type {
223: 				case llm.PartTypeText, llm.PartTypeReasoning:
224: 					text += p.Text
225: 				case llm.PartTypeToolCall:
226: 					inputBytes, _ := json.Marshal(p.Input)
227: 					toolCalls = append(toolCalls, openai.ChatCompletionMessageToolCallParam{
228: 						ID: p.ToolCallID,
229: 						Function: openai.ChatCompletionMessageToolCallFunctionParam{
230: 							Name:      p.ToolName,
231: 							Arguments: string(inputBytes),
232: 						},
233: 					})
234: 				}
235: 			}
236: 			if len(toolCalls) > 0 {
237: 				out = append(out, openai.ChatCompletionMessageParamUnion{
238: 					OfAssistant: &openai.ChatCompletionAssistantMessageParam{
239: 						Content:   openai.ChatCompletionAssistantMessageParamContentUnion{OfString: openai.String(text)},
240: 						ToolCalls: toolCalls,
241: 					},
242: 				})
243: 			} else {
244: 				out = append(out, openai.AssistantMessage(text))
245: 			}
246: 
247: 		case llm.RoleTool:
248: 			for _, p := range m.Content {
249: 				if p.Type != llm.PartTypeToolResult {
250: 					continue
251: 				}
252: 				resultText := ""
253: 				if p.Result != nil {
254: 					switch v := p.Result.Value.(type) {
255: 					case string:
256: 						resultText = v
257: 					default:
258: 						b, _ := json.Marshal(p.Result.Value)
259: 						resultText = string(b)
260: 					}
261: 				}
262: 				out = append(out, openai.ToolMessage(resultText, p.ToolCallID))
263: 			}
264: 		}
265: 	}
266: 	return out, nil
267: }

269: func extractText(parts []llm.ContentPart) string {
270: 	text := ""
271: 	for _, p := range parts {
272: 		if p.Type == llm.PartTypeText {
273: 			text += p.Text
274: 		}
275: 	}
276: 	return text
277: }

283: // runStream processes the OpenAI streaming response and emits canonical events.
284: //
285: // Usage handling: with stream_options.include_usage=true, the provider sends
286: // a final chunk with choices=[] and usage={...} AFTER the finish_reason chunk.
287: // We defer EventStepFinish until we've seen that usage chunk (or the stream ends),
288: // so that usage is always populated when the event is emitted.
289: func runStream(ctx context.Context, providerID string, stream *ssestream.Stream[openai.ChatCompletionChunk], out chan<- llm.Event) {
290: 	defer stream.Close()
291: 
292: 	out <- llm.Event{Type: llm.EventRequestStart}
293: 	out <- llm.Event{Type: llm.EventStepStart}
294: 
295: 	type toolState struct {
296: 		id      string
297: 		name    string
298: 		args    []byte
299: 		started bool // true once EventToolInputStart has been emitted
300: 	}
301: 	toolByIndex := map[int64]*toolState{}
302: 	inText := false
303: 
304: 	var usage llm.TokenUsage
305: 
306: 	// pendingFinish holds a StepFinish event whose usage may still be arriving.
307: 	// It is flushed when the usage chunk arrives or the stream ends.
308: 	var pendingFinish *llm.Event
309: 
310: 	flushPending := func() {
311: 		if pendingFinish != nil {
312: 			pendingFinish.Usage = usage
313: 			out <- *pendingFinish
314: 			pendingFinish = nil
315: 		}
316: 	}
317: 
318: 	for stream.Next() {
319: 		chunk := stream.Current()
320: 
321: 		// Usage-only chunk (choices=[]) — sent by providers after the finish chunk
322: 		// when stream_options.include_usage=true is set.
323: 		if len(chunk.Choices) == 0 {
324: 			if chunk.Usage.TotalTokens > 0 || chunk.JSON.Usage.Valid() {
325: 				usage.Input = int(chunk.Usage.PromptTokens)
326: 				usage.Output = int(chunk.Usage.CompletionTokens)
327: 				usage.Total = int(chunk.Usage.TotalTokens)
328: 			}
329: 			// Now that we have usage, flush the deferred StepFinish.
330: 			flushPending()
331: 			continue
332: 		}
333: 
334: 		choice := chunk.Choices[0]
335: 		delta := choice.Delta
336: 
337: 		if delta.Content != "" {
338: 			if !inText {
339: 				out <- llm.Event{Type: llm.EventTextStart}
340: 				inText = true
341: 			}
342: 			out <- llm.Event{Type: llm.EventTextDelta, Text: delta.Content}
343: 		}
344: 
345: 		// Also capture inline usage if the provider sends it alongside choices.
346: 		if chunk.Usage.TotalTokens > 0 {
347: 			usage.Input = int(chunk.Usage.PromptTokens)
348: 			usage.Output = int(chunk.Usage.CompletionTokens)
349: 			usage.Total = int(chunk.Usage.TotalTokens)
350: 		}
351: 
352: 		for _, tc := range delta.ToolCalls {
353: 			idx := tc.Index
354: 			ts, exists := toolByIndex[idx]
355: 			if !exists {
356: 				ts = &toolState{id: tc.ID, name: tc.Function.Name}
357: 				toolByIndex[idx] = ts
358: 			}
359: 			if tc.ID != "" && ts.id == "" {
360: 				ts.id = tc.ID
361: 			}
362: 			if tc.Function.Name != "" && ts.name == "" {
363: 				ts.name = tc.Function.Name
364: 			}
365: 			// Emit EventToolInputStart once both id and name are known.
366: 			// Deferred here to handle providers that send an empty id on the
367: 			// first delta and fill it in a subsequent one.
368: 			if !ts.started && ts.id != "" && ts.name != "" {
369: 				ts.started = true
370: 				out <- llm.Event{
371: 					Type:       llm.EventToolInputStart,
372: 					ToolCallID: ts.id,
373: 					ToolName:   ts.name,
374: 				}
375: 				// Replay any argument bytes that arrived before we had an ID.
376: 				if len(ts.args) > 0 {
377: 					out <- llm.Event{
378: 						Type:       llm.EventToolInputDelta,
379: 						ToolCallID: ts.id,
380: 						ToolName:   ts.name,
381: 						Text:       string(ts.args),
382: 					}
383: 				}
384: 			}
385: 			if tc.Function.Arguments != "" {
386: 				ts.args = append(ts.args, tc.Function.Arguments...)
387: 				// Only emit delta if we've already sent EventToolInputStart;
388: 				// otherwise the args are buffered in ts.args and will be
389: 				// replayed in the block above when the ID arrives.
390: 				if ts.started {
391: 					out <- llm.Event{
392: 						Type:       llm.EventToolInputDelta,
393: 						ToolCallID: ts.id,
394: 						ToolName:   ts.name,
395: 						Text:       tc.Function.Arguments,
396: 					}
397: 				}
398: 			}
399: 		}
400: 
401: 		if choice.FinishReason != "" {
402: 			if inText {
403: 				out <- llm.Event{Type: llm.EventTextEnd}
404: 				inText = false
405: 			}
406: 
407: 			// Finalise all tool calls.
408: 			for _, ts := range toolByIndex {
409: 				var input any
410: 				if len(ts.args) > 0 {
411: 					_ = json.Unmarshal(ts.args, &input)
412: 				}
413: 				out <- llm.Event{
414: 					Type:       llm.EventToolCall,
415: 					ToolCallID: ts.id,
416: 					ToolName:   ts.name,
417: 					Input:      input,
418: 				}
419: 			}
420: 			toolByIndex = map[int64]*toolState{}
421: 
422: 			// Defer StepFinish: usage may arrive in the next chunk.
423: 			ev := llm.Event{
424: 				Type:         llm.EventStepFinish,
425: 				Usage:        usage, // may be zero; updated when usage chunk arrives
426: 				FinishReason: mapFinishReason(string(choice.FinishReason)),
427: 			}
428: 			pendingFinish = &ev
429: 		}
430: 
431: 		select {
432: 		case <-ctx.Done():
433: 			out <- llm.Event{Type: llm.EventError, Err: ctx.Err()}
434: 			return
435: 		default:
436: 		}
437: 	}
438: 
439: 	if err := stream.Err(); err != nil {
440: 		out <- llm.Event{Type: llm.EventError, Err: classifyError(providerID, err)}
441: 		return
442: 	}
443: 
444: 	// Flush any deferred StepFinish (usage chunk may have been last or absent).
445: 	flushPending()
446: 
447: 	out <- llm.Event{
448: 		Type:         llm.EventRequestFinish,
449: 		Usage:        usage,
450: 		FinishReason: llm.FinishReasonStop,
451: 	}
452: }
453: 
454: func mapFinishReason(reason string) llm.FinishReason {
455: 	switch reason {
456: 	case "stop":
457: 		return llm.FinishReasonStop
458: 	case "tool_calls", "function_call":
459: 		return llm.FinishReasonToolCalls
460: 	case "length", "max_tokens":
461: 		return llm.FinishReasonLength
462: 	case "content_filter":
463: 		return llm.FinishReasonError
464: 	}
465: 	return llm.FinishReasonOther
466: }
467: 
468: func classifyError(providerID string, err error) error {
469: 	if err == nil {
470: 		return nil
471: 	}
472: 	var apiErr *openai.Error
473: 	if errors.As(err, &apiErr) {
474: 		headers := http.Header{}
475: 		if apiErr.Response != nil {
476: 			headers = apiErr.Response.Header
477: 		}
478: 		return llm.ClassifyHTTPError(providerID, int(apiErr.StatusCode), apiErr.Error(), headers)
479: 	}
480: 	return &llm.LLMError{
481: 		Kind:        llm.ErrTransport,
482: 		Message:     err.Error(),
483: 		IsRetryable: false,
484: 	}
485: }

Tools.name: glob
Tools.description:
Fast file pattern matching tool that works with any codebase size.
Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts".
Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.
Use this tool when you need to find files by name patterns.
When you are doing an open-ended search that may require multiple rounds of globbing and grepping, use the Task tool instead.
You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. It is always better to speculatively perform multiple searches as a batch that are potentially useful.

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

Tools.name: grep
Tools.description:
Fast content search tool that works with any codebase size.
Searches file contents using regular expressions.
Supports full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+").
Filter files by pattern with the include parameter (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}").
Returns file paths and line numbers with at least one match sorted by modification time.

include.description: File glob pattern to restrict search (e.g. "*.go", "*.{ts,tsx}").

path.description: Directory or file to search in. Defaults to the current working directory.

pattern.description: The regex pattern to search for in file contents.

Tools.name: read
Tools.description:
Read a file or directory from the local filesystem.
- Returns file contents with line numbers prefixed as "<n>: <content>".
- Supports text files, images (jpeg/png/gif/webp), and PDFs — images and PDFs are returned as binary attachments.
- Use offset and limit for pagination of large files (default limit: 2000 lines).
- For directories, lists entries one per line with trailing "/" for subdirectories.

filePath.description: The absolute path to the file or directory to read.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

offset.description: 1-indexed line number to start reading from. Defaults to 1.

Tools.name: write
Tools.description:
Write a file to the local filesystem, creating or overwriting it.
- The filePath must be an absolute path.
- Intermediate directories are created automatically.
- Prefer editing existing files with the edit tool when only partial changes are needed.
- Only create new files when explicitly required.

content.description: The full content to write to the file.

filePath.description: The absolute path to the file to write.

Tools.name: edit
Tools.description:
Perform exact string replacements in files.
- You must read the file at least once before editing to know the exact content.
- oldString must match the file content exactly (including whitespace and indentation).
- If oldString appears multiple times, provide more surrounding context to make it unique.
- Set replaceAll to true to rename a variable or replace every occurrence.
- If oldString is empty the file is created/overwritten with newString (same as write tool).

filePath.description: The absolute path to the file to modify.

oldString.description: The text to find and replace. Must match exactly.

replaceAll.description: Replace all occurrences of oldString. Default false.

Tools.name: bash
Tools.description:
Executes a given bash command in a persistent shell session with optional timeout.
- Use && to chain sequential commands that depend on each other.
- Use the workdir parameter instead of cd commands.
- Avoid interactive commands; stdin is always closed.
- Do not use find, grep, cat, head, tail, sed, awk when dedicated tools are available.
- Quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in 5-10 words.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 120000 ms (2m0s).

workdir.description: Working directory for the command. Defaults to the project root. Use this instead of cd commands.

Tools.name: knowledge_search
Tools.description: Search for information across configured knowledge sources. Returns a ranked list of titles and short snippets. Use knowledge_fetch with a result's ref_id to retrieve the full content of a specific item.

filters.description: Optional key-value filters passed to the source (field names depend on the backend).

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5).

query.description: The search terms or query expression.

Tools.name: knowledge_fetch
Tools.description: Fetch the full content of a knowledge item by its ref_id. Use ref_id values returned by knowledge_search. Returns the complete document body, which may be large.

ref_id.description: The ref_id of the item to fetch, as returned by knowledge_search.

Tools.name: session_reset
Tools.description:
Reset the current session: completely forget all conversation history, tool results, and compacted summaries. The session ID is preserved so you can continue in the same session after the reset.

IMPORTANT: Before calling this tool you MUST explicitly warn the user that all history will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered, and obtain their clear confirmation. Do not call this tool unless the user has confirmed.

events.text:
现在我有了全面的视角，来系统评价错误处理。

---

## 错误处理分析

总体来说，错误处理是**有层次设计的**，但存在几个值得关注的问题。

---

### 一、设计得好的部分

**1. 错误分类层（`llm/error.go`）**

这是整个系统最扎实的部分。`LLMError` 携带 `Kind`、`StatusCode`、`IsRetryable`、`ResponseHeaders` 四个维度，调用方不需要字符串匹配，只需检查 `Kind`。`errors.As` 链式查找让跨层传递不丢失类型信息。

**2. Provider 层错误处理对称**

Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的 `classifyError()` 结构完全一致——先 `errors.As` 匹配 SDK 的原生 error 类型，提取 HTTP 状态码和 header；无法识别的统一包装为 `ErrTransport`。这保证了上层（`Client`）收到的永远是 `*LLMError`，而不是裸的 SDK error。

**3. `tool.Fail` vs 普通 error 的两级语义**

`processor.go:352-358` 明确区分了两种工具错误：
```go
if tf, ok := tool.IsToolFailure(err); ok {
    _ = s.updateToolStatus(ctx, partID, store.ToolStatusError, nil, tf.Message)
} else {
    _ = s.updateToolStatus(ctx, partID, store.ToolStatusError, nil, err.Error())
}
```
`tool.Fail()` 产生的错误只影响单个工具调用，LLM 看到 error result 并继续；其他 error 走相同路径（也是 ToolStatusError），并不会直接 stop session。**但注意**：这里两种情况走的是同一个分支（都写 `ToolStatusError`），实际差别只是 message 来源。真正 stop session 的是 `executeTool` 的调用方——`processor.go` 里 `executeTool` 是 goroutine，错误不向上传播，session 不会因单个工具失败而停止。这个设计是对的。

**4. `cleanup()` 使用 `context.Background()`**

```go
func (s *processorState) cleanup() {
    ctx := context.Background()
```

这是一个重要的正确决策。cancel 触发后 caller 的 ctx 已经 Done，用它写 store 会导致所有 UpdatePart 静默失败，tool part 永久停留在 pending 状态。用 `context.Background()` 确保清理操作总能完成。

**5. 压缩时使用 `context.WithoutCancel`**

```go
// compaction.go:254
ctx = context.WithoutCancel(ctx)
```

防止 SSE 客户端断开时压缩摘要 LLM 调用被中断，留下半完成的压缩状态。设计上考虑到了。

---

### 二、明显的问题

**1. store 错误被大量 `_ =` 忽略**

这是整个代码库里最普遍的问题。`processor.go` 中几乎所有 store 写操作都忽略了错误：

```go
// processor.go:215, 221, 238, 244, 279, 284, 305, 311, 328...
_ = s.updateTextPart(ctx, s.currentTextPartID, ...)
_ = s.updateReasoningPart(ctx, ...)
_ = s.updateToolStatus(ctx, partID, ...)
_, _ = s.createPart(ctx, store.PartTypeStepFinish, ...)
```

`createPart` 的错误在 `EventToolInputStart` 处理中是被返回的（`processor.go:259`），但 `updateTextPart`、`updateReasoningPart`、`updateToolCompleted` 的失败全部静默丢弃。对于内存 store 来说无害，但如果换 SQLite 后端出现磁盘满/锁超时，这些错误会完全不可见，用户看到的是正常响应但数据没有保存。

**2. `isAlreadyInterrupted` 使用 `context.Background()` 但方式可疑**

```go
// processor.go:367-377
func isAlreadyInterrupted(s store.Store, partID string) bool {
    p, err := s.GetPart(context.Background(), partID)
    if err != nil {
        return false  // ← 读取失败时静默返回 false
    }
    ...
}
```

GetPart 失败（网络抖动、DB 错误）时返回 `false`，导致 `executeTool` 继续执行并覆盖 cleanup 的 interrupted 标记。这个竞态窗口虽然很窄，但行为与预期相反——读取失败应该保守地阻止覆盖，而不是放行。

**3. JSON 解析错误被静默丢弃（两处）**

```go
// anthropic.go:345
_ = json.Unmarshal(toolInputBuf, &input)

// openai.go:411
_ = json.Unmarshal(ts.args, &input)
```

工具参数的 JSON 解析失败时，`input` 为 `nil`，工具拿到的是空参数，执行结果完全错误。正确处理应该是发送 `EventToolError` 而不是继续传递 nil input。这个静默失败会让工具以错误参数执行，LLM 可能陷入反复重试的循环。

**4. `openai.go` 中另一个被忽略的 JSON 错误**

```go
// openai.go:148
_ = json.Unmarshal(schemaBytes, &schemaMap)
```

工具 schema 反序列化失败时 `schemaMap` 为 nil，发给 OpenAI 的工具定义是空的，调用会静默失败或产生不可预期的行为。

**5. `compaction.go` 中两处 `_ =` 不对称**

```go
// compaction.go:384-386（step 6）
_ = c.store.CreatePart(ctx, &store.Part{...})

// compaction.go:398-401
if bm, readErr := c.store.GetMessage(ctx, compactionMsgID); readErr == nil {
    bm.Tokens.Input = len(excerpt) / 4
    _ = c.store.UpdateMessage(ctx, bm)  // ← 忽略
}
```

Step 6 的注释说"Non-fatal"，忽略是有意图的，但没有日志。如果 CreatePart 失败，下次压缩时 `RecentContext` excerpt 会丢失，但没有任何可观测性。

**6. `Prune` 的错误阈值逻辑存在 bug**

```go
// compaction.go:712
if totalPruned < PruneMinimum/4 {
    return fmt.Errorf("prune: not enough content to prune (%d estimated tokens)", totalPruned)
}
```

`PruneMinimum = 20_000`（token），但 `totalPruned` 统计的是 `len(d.Output) / 4`（字符→token 估算）。然后比较 `totalPruned < 20_000/4 = 5_000`。这把一个已经是估算值的量再除以 4，阈值实际上是 5000 个估算 token，等效于大约 80KB 的工具输出，逻辑意图模糊。

**7. `markAssistantCancelled` 的竞态注释承认了但没有修复**

```go
// prompt.go:498-500
// Known race: cleanup() inside Process() waits up to 250ms for tool goroutines.
// After that timeout, goroutines may still be running and could write
// ToolStatusCompleted after ListParts reads here.
```

代码注释承认了这个问题，但标注为"future work"。结果是：取消后 250ms 内完成的工具调用，其结果可能被错误地标记为 `Cancelled` 而不是 `Interrupted`，导致该轮次的工具结果对 LLM 不可见。

---

### 三、总结

| 层 | 评价 |
|---|---|
| `llm/error.go` 错误分类 | 扎实，覆盖全面 |
| `client.go` 重试 | 设计正确，mid-stream 重试不泄漏半截数据 |
| `provider/` 错误转换 | 对称，但 JSON 解析错误被忽略 |
| `session/processor.go` | store 写错误大量 `_ =` 忽略 |
| `session/compaction.go` | 关键路径（step 4）处理正确，非关键路径缺日志 |
| `session/prompt.go` | 取消竞态有文档但未修复 |

最需要修复的两个问题：

1. **provider 层 JSON 解析失败** — `json.Unmarshal` 的 `_ =` 应改为发送 `EventToolError`
2. **`isAlreadyInterrupted` 读取失败时的保守策略** — 失败时应返回 `true`（保守），而不是 `false`（放行覆盖）

1: # llm-go
2: 
3: A Go port of the LLM handling layer from [opencode](https://github.com/sst/opencode).
4: Provides streaming LLM conversations, agentic tool-call orchestration, automatic
5: context compaction, and a pluggable knowledge retrieval system — all as composable
6: Go packages.
7: 
8: ```
9: github.com/larryhou/llm-go
10: ```
11: 
12: ---
13: 
14: ## Features
15: 
16: - **Streaming client with retry** — provider-agnostic `llm.Provider` interface;
17:   automatic retry with exponential back-off on transient errors; mid-stream error
18:   recovery without losing buffered events.
19: 
20: - **Two provider adapters** — `provider/anthropic` (official SDK) and
21:   `provider/openai` (OpenAI-compatible, works with any proxy or local endpoint).
22: 
23: - **Full agentic loop** (`session.RunLoop`) — user message → LLM stream →
24:   parallel tool execution → tool results back to LLM → repeat until `stop`.
25: 
26: - **Context compaction** — when the session approaches the model's context limit,
27:   the oldest turns are summarised by a second LLM call and replaced by a compact
28:   summary, then the conversation continues seamlessly.
29: 
30: - **Doom-loop detection** — stops the loop when the same tool is called with
31:   identical arguments three consecutive times.
32: 
33: - **Pluggable knowledge retrieval** (`knowledge.Manager`) — register any number
34:   of `Source` backends; the manager dispatches `knowledge_search` and
35:   `knowledge_fetch` as native `tool.Tool` calls, with priority grouping,
36:   concurrent dispatch per group, and automatic fallback.
37: 
38: - **Bleve full-text source** — ready-made `knowledge/source/bleve` backed by
39:   an in-memory or on-disk Bleve index.
40: 
41: - **HTTP knowledge API** (`cmd/llm-api`) — self-contained HTTP server
42:   that indexes a skills directory, exposes REST search/fetch endpoints, and
43:   streams LLM chat responses as Server-Sent Events.
44: 
45: - **opencode-compatible config** — reads `~/.config/llm/llm.json` and
46:   `.llm/llm.json`; schema mirrors opencode's `opencode.json`.
47: 
48: ---
49:

51:

55: ├── provider/

57: │   ├── anthropic/        Anthropic Messages API (anthropic-sdk-go)
58: │   └── openai/           OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions (openai-go)

61: │   ├── processor.go      Event handler — tool lifecycle, doom-loop, overflow
62: │   ├── compaction.go     Compact() / Prune() / Select() / FilterCompacted()
63: │   ├── context.go        ToModelMessages() — store records → llm.Message

114:     })

196: ### 3. Cancellable turns with `RunLoopAsync`
197: 
198: `RunLoop` is synchronous and blocks until the turn completes. `RunLoopAsync`
199: returns a `*RunHandle` immediately, allowing the caller to cancel an in-flight
200: turn and start a new one without waiting for the old one to fully clean up.
201: 
202: **`RunHandle` fields:**
203: 
204: | Field | Description |
205: |-------|-------------|
206: | `Done <-chan struct{}` | Closed after full cleanup including Prune |
207: | `StoreDone <-chan struct{}` | Closed once store writes are complete (before Prune) — sufficient for the next turn to start safely |
208: | `Result RunResult` | Available after `<-Done` |
209: | `Err error` | Available after `<-Done` |
210: 
211: ```go
212: // Start a turn asynchronously.
213: h := session.RunLoopAsync(ctx, st, session.RunInput{
214:     SessionID: sessID,
215:     UserMsg:   "What is 123 * 456?",
216:     Model:     model,
217:     Provider:  prov,
218:     Tools:     []tool.Tool{calcTool{}},
219: })
220: 
221: // Cancel the turn (e.g. user pressed ESC or sent a new message).
222: h.Cancel()
223: <-h.Done // wait for full cleanup before reusing the session
224: 
225: // --- OR: start a new turn immediately, passing StoreDone as WaitFor.
226: // The new turn's goroutine starts right away but waits internally on
227: // prev.StoreDone before writing to the store, so no orphan records are
228: // created and history is always consistent.
229: h2 := session.RunLoopAsync(ctx, st, session.RunInput{
230:     SessionID: sessID,
231:     UserMsg:   "Actually, what is 789 * 321?",
232:     Model:     model,
233:     Provider:  prov,
234:     Tools:     []tool.Tool{calcTool{}},
235:     WaitFor:   h.StoreDone, // wait for store consistency, not full Prune
236: })
237: <-h2.Done
238: ```
239: 
240: **Typical HTTP server pattern** (cancel previous turn on new message):
241: 
242: ```go
243: var mu sync.Mutex
244: var activeHandle *session.RunHandle
245: 
246: func handleChat(userMsg string) {
247:     mu.Lock()
248:     prev := activeHandle
249:     if prev != nil {
250:         prev.Cancel()
251:     }
252:     var waitFor <-chan struct{}
253:     if prev != nil {
254:         waitFor = prev.StoreDone
255:     }
256:     h := session.RunLoopAsync(ctx, st, session.RunInput{
257:         SessionID: sessID,
258:         UserMsg:   userMsg,
259:         Model:     model,
260:         Provider:  prov,
261:         WaitFor:   waitFor,
262:     })
263:     activeHandle = h
264:     mu.Unlock()
265: 
266:     <-h.Done // keep SSE connection open until turn finishes
267: }
268: ```
269: 
270: Holding `mu` across `Cancel + RunLoopAsync + activeHandle =` ensures a third
271: concurrent request cannot observe a stale previous handle and race on the same
272: `StoreDone`.

315: `session_reset` lets the LLM wipe the session on user request.

356:     compactionHook := historySrc.Hook() // cache the hook, don't call Hook() per turn
357: 
358:     // 2. Knowledge manager — register static source at priority 1, history at 0.
359:     idx, _ := bleve.NewMemOnly(bleve.NewIndexMapping())
360:     km := knowledge.NewManager(knowledge.ManagerConfig{
361:         SourceTimeout: 5 * time.Second,
362:         MaxResults:    5,
363:         SnippetMaxChars: 300,
364:         ContentMaxChars: 8000,
365:     })
366:     km.Register(blevesrc.New(idx, "docs", 1, nil))
367:     km.Register(historySrc) // history has higher priority (0)
368: 
369:     // 3. session_reset tool — resetFn is called atomically.
370:     //    If a server-level lock is needed (concurrent requests), hold it here.
371:     resetTool := session.NewResetTool(func(resetCtx context.Context) error {
372:         if err := st.DeleteSession(resetCtx, sessID); err != nil {
373:             return err
374:         }
375:         if err := st.CreateSession(resetCtx, &store.Session{
376:             ID: sessID, Model: "openai/gpt-4o",
377:         }); err != nil {
378:             return err
379:         }
380:         return historySrc.Reset() // wipes the Bleve index
381:     })
382: 
383:     // 4. Build tool list — explicit make avoids aliasing km.Tools() backing array.
384:     kmTools := km.Tools()
385:     tools := make([]tool.Tool, 0, len(kmTools)+1)
386:     tools = append(tools, kmTools...)
387:     tools = append(tools, resetTool)
388: 
389:     // 5. RunLoop — pass OnCompact so compacted turns are indexed automatically.
390:     for _, msg := range []string{
391:         "Explain context compaction.",
392:         "What did we discuss earlier?", // LLM may call knowledge_search here
393:     } {
394:         _, err := session.RunLoop(ctx, st, session.RunInput{
395:             SessionID: sessID,
396:             UserMsg:   msg,
397:             Model:     model,
398:             Provider:  prov,
399:             Tools:     tools,
400:             OnCompact: compactionHook, // nil = no history indexing
401:         })
402:         if err != nil {
403:             fmt.Fprintf(nil, "error: %v\n", err)
404:         }
405:     }
406: }
407: ```
408: 
409: **Key rules:**
410: - Create `SessionHistorySource` and call `Hook()` **once per session**, not per turn.
411: - Register `historySrc` at a **lower priority number** than static knowledge sources.
412: - Build `tools` with explicit `make` + `append` — do not `append(km.Tools(), ...)` directly.
413: - The `resetFn` must cover `DeleteSession` + `CreateSession` + `historySrc.Reset()` atomically.
414: - `OnCompact: nil` disables history indexing silently — no hook call, no error.
415: 
416: ### 6. Run the llm-api HTTP server
417: 
418: ```bash
419: # Start — indexes .opencode/skills and listens on :7700
420: go run ./cmd/llm-api/ \
421:     -skills /path/to/.opencode/skills \
422:     -addr   127.0.0.1:7700 \
423:     -llm-url https://api.openai.com/v1 \
424:     -llm-key sk-your-api-key \
425:     -model  gpt-4o
426: 
427: # Health check
428: curl http://127.0.0.1:7700/health
429: # → {"status":"ok","doc_count":3,"session_count":0}
430: 
431: # Search the knowledge index
432: curl "http://127.0.0.1:7700/search?q=context+compaction&max_results=3"
433: 
434: # Chat with SSE streaming (session persists across requests)
435: curl -sN -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7700/chat \
436:     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
437:     -d '{"message":"Explain how context compaction works."}'
438: 
439: # Continue the same session
440: curl -sN -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7700/chat \
441:     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
442:     -d '{"message":"Give me a code example.","session_id":"sess-from-x-session-id-header"}'
443: 
444: # Inspect stored messages
445: curl http://127.0.0.1:7700/sessions/{session-id}/messages
446: ```
447: 
448: **SSE event format:**
449: 
450: ```
451: data: {"type":"text","delta":"Context compaction fires when..."}
452: data: {"type":"tool_call","tool":"knowledge_search","input":{"query":"compaction"}}
453: data: {"type":"tool_result","tool":"knowledge_search","output":"## Result 1\n..."}
454: data: {"type":"done","session_id":"sess-1234567890"}
455: ```

502: ## Testing
503: 
504: ### Unit tests (no network required)
505: 
506: ```bash
507: go test ./llm/... ./config/... ./session/... ./store/... ./tool/... ./knowledge/...
508: ```
509: 
510: ### Integration tests (requires a live LLM endpoint)
511: 
512: ```bash
513: export LLM_INTEGRATION=1
514: export TIMI_BASE_URL="http://your-llm-proxy/v1"
515: export TIMI_API_KEY="sk-your-key"
516: export TIMI_MODEL="claude-sonnet-4.6"
517: 
518: # Core integration tests
519: go test ./integration/... -v -count=1 -timeout=120s
520: 
521: # Context overflow + compaction end-to-end
522: go test ./integration/overflow/... -v -count=1 -timeout=300s
523: 
524: # Knowledge retrieval + LLM usage
525: go test ./integration/knowledge/... -v -count=1 -timeout=120s
526: ```

528: ### llm-api feature test (requires running server)
529: 
530: ```bash
531: go run ./cmd/llm-api/ -skills .opencode/skills -addr 127.0.0.1:7700 &
532: 
533: bash cmd/llm-api/test_features.sh
534: # → Passed: 32 / 32 — ALL TESTS PASSED
535: ```
536: 
537: The shell test covers: normal tool call, multi-turn memory, knowledge search/fetch,
538: recoverable tool failure, `max_steps` enforcement, stateful counters, context
539: compaction, async tool execution, all SSE event types, and session inspection.
540: 
541: ---
542: 
543: ## Key Design Decisions
544: 
545: **Provider-agnostic core** — `llm.Provider` is a single interface (`ID()` +
546: `Stream()`). Anthropic and OpenAI adapters translate their native SDK events into
547: the same canonical `llm.Event` stream. New providers implement one interface.
548: 
549: **Immediate turn handoff** — `RunHandle` exposes two channels: `StoreDone`
550: (closed once the current turn's store writes are complete, before Prune) and
551: `Done` (closed after full cleanup including Prune). A new turn can pass
552: `prev.StoreDone` as `RunInput.WaitFor` to start immediately without waiting
553: for Prune, while still guaranteeing a consistent store view. The user message
554: is written *after* `WaitFor` resolves, so a cancelled wait leaves no orphan
555: records.
556: 
557: **Compaction is transparent to the caller** — `RunLoop` detects overflow via
558: `IsOverflow(usage, model)` after every `EventStepFinish`. It calls `Compact()`
559: internally, inserts a summary message into the store, then retries the turn.
560: The caller sees no difference; the session simply continues.
561: 
562: **Tool failure vs. fatal error** — returning `tool.Fail("message")` from a
563: tool produces an error tool-result that the LLM receives and can reason about.
564: The session continues. Any other error stops the session immediately.
565: 
566: **Two-level knowledge retrieval** — `knowledge_search` calls `Source.Peek()`
567: and returns only snippets (minimal context growth). The LLM decides whether to
568: call `knowledge_fetch` with a `ref_id` to retrieve the full document. This keeps
569: the context window small by default.
570: 
571: **RefID routing** — every `Result.RefID` has the form `"{sourceID}:{key}"`.
572: The manager uses `strings.Cut` to route `knowledge_fetch` directly to the correct
573: source in O(1), avoiding a linear scan across all sources.
574: 
575: **SummaryProvider separation** — the compaction summary LLM call uses a separate
576: `SummaryProvider` (when provided). This prevents middleware (e.g., the SSE event
577: forwarder in `llm-api`) from leaking internal summary events to external
578: clients.
579: 
580: ---
581: 
582: ## Requirements
583: 
584: - Go 1.25+
585: - An OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic LLM endpoint
586: - No CGO required for the core library; Bleve's FAISS backend requires CGO if
587:   used (the in-memory Bleve index used by `llm-api` does not)
588: 
589: ---
590: 
591: ## Acknowledgements
592:

594: configuration schemas in this library are derived from and inspired by the
595: open-source project [**opencode**](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode).
596: The original TypeScript implementation can be found at
597: `packages/opencode/src/session/` in that repository.

了解，以下是 llm-go 的概览：

## llm-go 项目概览

`llm-go` 是 [opencode](https://github.com/sst/opencode) LLM 层的 Go 移植版本，模块路径为 `github.com/larryhou/llm-go`。

### 核心功能

| 功能 | 说明 |
|------|------|
| **流式客户端** | provider-agnostic `llm.Provider` 接口，带指数退避重试 |
| **双 Provider** | `provider/anthropic` 和 `provider/openai`（兼容所有 OpenAI-compatible 端点） |
| **完整 agentic loop** | `session.RunLoop()` — 用户消息 → LLM 流式输出 → 并行工具执行 → 工具结果回传 → 循环直到 `stop` |
| **Context 压缩** | 接近上下文限制时自动摘要旧轮次，对调用方透明 |
| **Doom-loop 检测** | 同一工具以相同参数连续调用 3 次时停止循环 |
| **知识检索** | `knowledge.Manager` 支持多 `Source` 后端，two-level 检索（先 snippet，再 full doc） |
| **Bleve 全文索引** | `knowledge/source/bleve`，支持内存或磁盘索引 |
| **HTTP API** | `cmd/llm-api` — SSE 流式 chat + REST 搜索端点 |

### 包结构

```
llm/          — 核心类型、错误分类、重试
provider/     — Anthropic / OpenAI 适配器
session/      — RunLoop、compaction、context 转换
tool/         — Tool 接口、Registry、结果截断
store/        — Session/Message/Part CRUD 接口
knowledge/    — Manager、Source 接口、Bleve 实现
config/       — 配置加载
auth/         — auth.json 读写
cmd/          — llm-api HTTP 服务、index-skills CLI
```

### 关键设计决策

- **`RunHandle`** 暴露两个 channel：`StoreDone`（store 写完）和 `Done`（完整清理），支持即时 turn 切换
- **RefID 路由**：`{sourceID}:{key}` 格式，O(1) 定位目标 source
- **`SummaryProvider` 分离**：压缩摘要调用使用独立 provider，避免内部事件泄漏给外部客户端
- **工具失败 vs 致命错误**：`tool.Fail()` 让 LLM 收到错误结果并继续；其他错误立即终止

1: // Package llm defines the Provider interface and core streaming client.
2: package llm
3: 
4: import (
5: 	"context"
6: 	"time"
7: )
8: 
9: // Provider is the abstraction over a specific LLM provider (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.).
10: // Implementations live in provider/anthropic and provider/openai.
11: type Provider interface {
12: 	// ID returns the provider identifier (e.g. "anthropic", "openai").
13: 	ID() string
14: 
15: 	// Stream sends a request and returns a channel of events.
16: 	// The channel is closed when the stream ends or an error occurs.
17: 	// Callers must drain the channel until it's closed.
18: 	// Cancelling ctx aborts the stream.
19: 	Stream(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan Event, error)
20: }
21: 
22: // Client wraps a Provider and adds retry logic.
23: type Client struct {
24: 	provider   Provider
25: 	maxRetries int
26: }
27: 
28: // NewClient creates a new Client wrapping the given Provider.
29: func NewClient(p Provider) *Client {
30: 	return &Client{provider: p, maxRetries: 5}
31: }
32: 
33: // Stream starts an LLM stream with automatic retry on retryable errors.
34: // Returns a channel of events; closed when the stream finishes or fatally errors.
35: func (c *Client) Stream(ctx context.Context, req Request) <-chan Event {
36: 	ch := make(chan Event, 32)
37: 	go func() {
38: 		defer close(ch)
39: 		c.streamWithRetry(ctx, req, ch)
40: 	}()
41: 	return ch
42: }
43: 
44: func (c *Client) streamWithRetry(ctx context.Context, req Request, out chan<- Event) {
45: 	for attempt := 1; attempt <= c.maxRetries; attempt++ {
46: 		retry, done := c.doStream(ctx, req, out, attempt)
47: 		if done {
48: 			return
49: 		}
50: 		if !retry {
51: 			return
52: 		}
53: 		// retry — caller provided a delay already via retryErr.ResponseHeaders
54: 	}
55: }
56: 
57: // doStream runs one streaming attempt.
58: // Returns (shouldRetry, isDone).
59: func (c *Client) doStream(ctx context.Context, req Request, out chan<- Event, attempt int) (bool, bool) {
60: 	events, err := c.provider.Stream(ctx, req)
61: 	if err != nil {
62: 		if llmErr, ok := AsLLMError(err); ok && ShouldRetry(llmErr) && attempt < c.maxRetries {
63: 			if !c.sleep(ctx, RetryDelay(attempt, llmErr.ResponseHeaders)) {
64: 				out <- Event{Type: EventError, Err: ctx.Err()}
65: 				return false, true
66: 			}
67: 			return true, false
68: 		}
69: 		out <- Event{Type: EventError, Err: err}
70: 		return false, true
71: 	}
72: 
73: 	// Buffer all events from this attempt; only flush to out once we receive
74: 	// EventRequestFinish. On retry, discard the buffer so the caller never
75: 	// sees a partial sequence from a failed attempt.
76: 	var buf []Event
77: 	var retryErr *LLMError
78: 	for ev := range events {
79: 		if ev.Type == EventError {
80: 			if llmErr, ok := AsLLMError(ev.Err); ok && ShouldRetry(llmErr) && attempt < c.maxRetries {
81: 				retryErr = llmErr
82: 				// drain remaining events from provider
83: 				for range events {
84: 				}
85: 				break
86: 			}
87: 			// Fatal error — flush buffer then send error so caller gets context.
88: 			for _, buffered := range buf {
89: 				out <- buffered
90: 			}
91: 			out <- ev
92: 			return false, true
93: 		}
94: 		buf = append(buf, ev)
95: 		if ev.Type == EventRequestFinish {
96: 			for _, buffered := range buf {
97: 				out <- buffered
98: 			}
99: 			return false, true
100: 		}
101: 	}
102: 
103: 	if retryErr != nil {
104: 		if !c.sleep(ctx, RetryDelay(attempt, retryErr.ResponseHeaders)) {
105: 			out <- Event{Type: EventError, Err: ctx.Err()}
106: 			return false, true
107: 		}
108: 		return true, false
109: 	}
110: 	return false, true
111: }
112: 
113: // sleep waits for d or until ctx is cancelled. Returns false if ctx was cancelled.
114: func (c *Client) sleep(ctx context.Context, d time.Duration) bool {
115: 	select {
116: 	case <-ctx.Done():
117: 		return false
118: 	case <-time.After(d):
119: 		return true
120: 	}
121: }

171: 	if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "<!") || strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "<html") {
172: 		switch statusCode {

174: 			return "Unauthorized: check your API key"
175: 		case 403:
176: 			return "Forbidden: insufficient permissions"
177: 		default:

191: // RetryDelay calculates the delay before the next retry attempt.
192: // Aligned with packages/opencode/src/session/retry.ts delay().
193: //
194: // Priority:
195: //  1. retry-after-ms header (ms float)
196: //  2. retry-after header (seconds float or HTTP date)
197: //  3. Exponential backoff: 2000ms × 2^(attempt-1), capped at 30s
198: func RetryDelay(attempt int, headers http.Header) time.Duration {
199: 	if headers != nil {
200: 		if v := headers.Get("retry-after-ms"); v != "" {
201: 			if ms, err := strconv.ParseFloat(v, 64); err == nil && ms > 0 {
202: 				return time.Duration(ms) * time.Millisecond
203: 			}
204: 		}
205: 		if v := headers.Get("retry-after"); v != "" {
206: 			// Try as seconds
207: 			if secs, err := strconv.ParseFloat(v, 64); err == nil && secs > 0 {
208: 				return time.Duration(secs*1000) * time.Millisecond
209: 			}
210: 			// Try as HTTP date
211: 			if t, err := http.ParseTime(v); err == nil {
212: 				d := time.Until(t)
213: 				if d > 0 {
214: 					return d
215: 				}
216: 			}
217: 		}
218: 	}
219: 
220: 	// Exponential backoff: 2000 × 2^(attempt-1), max 30s
221: 	const (
222: 		initial = 2_000 * time.Millisecond
223: 		maxDelay = 30_000 * time.Millisecond
224: 	)
225: 	delay := initial
226: 	for i := 1; i < attempt; i++ {
227: 		delay *= 2
228: 		if delay > maxDelay {
229: 			return maxDelay
230: 		}
231: 	}
232: 	return delay
233: }

243: 	}
244: 	if err.StatusCode >= 500 {

1: // Package llm provides RecordProvider — a stateless transparent wrapper
2: // that appends one JSON record per Stream() call to a recording file.
3: //
4: // # Format
5: //
6: // The recording file is newline-delimited JSON (ndjson). Each line is one
7: // Record — the full request plus the filtered response events:
8: //
9: //	{"request":{...},"events":[{"type":"request-start"},{"type":"step-start"},{"type":"text-delta","text":"..."},{"type":"step-finish","finish_reason":"stop","usage":{"input":1234,"output":56}},{"type":"request-finish","finish_reason":"stop"}]}
10: //	{"request":{...},"events":[...]}
11: //
12: // One file covers the entire session lifetime. The replay provider reads the
13: // file and consumes one line per Stream() call, in order.
14: //
15: // Only semantically significant events are stored. Low-level lifecycle events
16: // (TextStart/End, ToolInputStart/Delta) are synthesised by the replay provider.
17: // EventStepFinish.Usage carries real token counts — critical for compaction.
18: package llm
19: 
20: import (
21: 	"context"
22: 	"encoding/json"
23: 	"fmt"
24: 	"os"
25: 	"sync"
26: )
27: 
28: // ── Types ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
29: 
30: // RecordEvent is a JSON-serialisable snapshot of one llm.Event.
31: type RecordEvent struct {
32: 	Type         EventType    `json:"type"`
33: 	Text         string       `json:"text,omitempty"`
34: 	Signature    string       `json:"signature,omitempty"`
35: 	ToolCallID   string       `json:"tool_call_id,omitempty"`
36: 	ToolName     string       `json:"tool_name,omitempty"`
37: 	Input        any          `json:"input,omitempty"`
38: 	FinishReason FinishReason `json:"finish_reason,omitempty"`
39: 	Usage        *TokenUsage  `json:"usage,omitempty"`
40: 	Error        string       `json:"error,omitempty"`
41: }
42: 
43: // Record is one line in the recording file: the request sent to the LLM
44: // and the significant response events.
45: type Record struct {
46: 	Request Request         `json:"request"`
47: 	Events  []RecordEvent `json:"events"`
48: }
49: 
50: // ── RecordProvider ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
51: 
52: // RecordProvider wraps a real Provider and appends one Record per
53: // Stream() call to path. It is fully transparent — no lifecycle methods, no
54: // turn-boundary logic. The file can be replayed with DebugProvider.
55: type RecordProvider struct {
56: 	inner Provider
57: 	mu    sync.Mutex
58: 	f     *os.File
59: 	enc   *json.Encoder
60: }
61: 
62: // NewRecordProvider wraps inner and records every Stream() call to path.
63: // The file is created (or truncated) immediately; an error is returned if it
64: // cannot be opened.
65: func NewRecordProvider(inner Provider, path string) (*RecordProvider, error) {
66: 	f, err := os.Create(path)
67: 	if err != nil {
68: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("recording: create %s: %w", path, err)
69: 	}
70: 	enc := json.NewEncoder(f)
71: 	enc.SetEscapeHTML(false)
72: 	return &RecordProvider{inner: inner, f: f, enc: enc}, nil
73: }
74: 
75: // ID satisfies llm.Provider.
76: func (p *RecordProvider) ID() string { return p.inner.ID() }
77: 
78: // Close flushes and closes the recording file.
79: func (p *RecordProvider) Close() error {
80: 	p.mu.Lock()
81: 	defer p.mu.Unlock()
82: 	return p.f.Close()
83: }
84: 
85: // Stream satisfies llm.Provider. It transparently proxies to the inner
86: // provider while recording the request and all significant response events.
87: // One Record is appended to the file when the stream closes.
88: func (p *RecordProvider) Stream(ctx context.Context, req Request) (<-chan Event, error) {
89: 	inner, err := p.inner.Stream(ctx, req)
90: 	if err != nil {
91: 		return nil, err
92: 	}
93: 
94: 	out := make(chan Event, 128)
95: 	go func() {
96: 		defer close(out)
97: 
98: 		step := Record{
99: 			Request: req,
100: 			Events:  []RecordEvent{{Type: EventRequestStart}},
101: 		}
102: 
103: 		for ev := range inner {
104: 			select {
105: 			case out <- ev:
106: 			case <-ctx.Done():
107: 				for range inner {
108: 				}
109: 				return
110: 			}
111: 			recordEvent(&step, ev)
112: 		}
113: 
114: 		p.mu.Lock()
115: 		_ = p.enc.Encode(step)
116: 		p.mu.Unlock()
117: 	}()
118: 
119: 	return out, nil
120: }
121: 
122: // recordEvent appends significant events to step, accumulating text/reasoning
123: // deltas into a single record per LLM step.
124: func recordEvent(step *Record, ev Event) {
125: 	switch ev.Type {
126: 	case EventStepStart:
127: 		step.Events = append(step.Events, RecordEvent{Type: EventStepStart})
128: 
129: 	case EventTextDelta:
130: 		accumulateDelta(step, EventTextDelta, ev.Text)
131: 
132: 	case EventReasoningDelta:
133: 		accumulateDelta(step, EventReasoningDelta, ev.Text)
134: 
135: 	case EventReasoningEnd:
136: 		step.Events = append(step.Events, RecordEvent{Type: EventReasoningEnd, Signature: ev.Signature})
137: 
138: 	case EventToolCall:
139: 		step.Events = append(step.Events, RecordEvent{
140: 			Type:       EventToolCall,
141: 			ToolName:   ev.ToolName,
142: 			ToolCallID: ev.ToolCallID,
143: 			Input:      ev.Input,
144: 		})
145: 
146: 	case EventStepFinish:
147: 		u := ev.Usage
148: 		step.Events = append(step.Events, RecordEvent{
149: 			Type:         EventStepFinish,
150: 			FinishReason: ev.FinishReason,
151: 			Usage:        &u,
152: 		})
153: 
154: 	case EventRequestFinish:
155: 		step.Events = append(step.Events, RecordEvent{
156: 			Type:         EventRequestFinish,
157: 			FinishReason: ev.FinishReason,
158: 		})
159: 
160: 	case EventError:
161: 		errStr := ""
162: 		if ev.Err != nil {
163: 			errStr = ev.Err.Error()
164: 		}
165: 		step.Events = append(step.Events, RecordEvent{Type: EventError, Error: errStr})
166: 	}
167: }
168: 
169: // accumulateDelta merges a text delta into the last matching RecordEvent within
170: // the current LLM step, or appends a new one if none exists yet.
171: func accumulateDelta(step *Record, t EventType, text string) {
172: 	for i := len(step.Events) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
173: 		if step.Events[i].Type == EventStepStart {
174: 			break
175: 		}
176: 		if step.Events[i].Type == t {
177: 			step.Events[i].Text += text
178: 			return
179: 		}
180: 	}
181: 	step.Events = append(step.Events, RecordEvent{Type: t, Text: text})
182: }
